entries.update: Hillary Clinton was deposed by the Republican-led House Oversight Committee on February 26 as part of an Epstein investigation, with Bill Clinton scheduled for deposition on February 27.

Hillary Clinton and Bill Clinton testified in closed-door sessions before the House Oversight Committee as part of its Epstein investigation, with Hillary Clinton stating she did not know Jeffrey Epstein and Bill Clinton testifying the day after. Neither has been accused of crimes related to Epstein.
The House Oversight Committee released video depositions of Bill and Hillary Clinton on Monday as part of its Jeffrey Epstein investigation. The depositions took place the week before their release.
The House Oversight Committee voted on a bipartisan basis to subpoena Attorney General Pam Bondi regarding the DOJ's handling of Jeffrey Epstein-related files.
The House Oversight Committee voted on a bipartisan basis to subpoena Attorney General Pam Bondi regarding the DOJ's handling of Jeffrey Epstein-related files.
The DOJ released previously withheld documents from the Epstein files, including FBI interview reports relating to allegations made against President Donald Trump by a woman.

Rep. James Comer and the House Oversight Committee are investigating the Epstein case. The federal government requested that New Mexico stop its investigation into Epstein's Zorro Ranch around 2019 during Trump's first term.
Richard Kahn, Jeffrey Epstein's accountant, testified before the House Oversight Committee; Epstein accumulated hundreds of millions of dollars over his career.

Tova Noel, a former prison guard at the Metropolitan Correctional Center who was on duty the night Jeffrey Epstein died, is scheduled to testify before the House Oversight Committee as part of an ongoing congressional investigation.

New documents are revealing Jeffrey Epstein's network of connections and relationships cultivated among powerful and elite circles in the original sex-trafficking investigation that originated in Florida.
Leon Black and his wife Debra purchased the property at 1111 Calle Vista Drive in Beverly Hills for $38 million in 2016, which was subsequently sold for $47 million.

Deputy Attorney General Todd Blanche dismissed suggestions that victims of convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein have been ignored by the Justice Department and defended the Trump administration's handling of the investigation.
Metropolitan Police chief Mark Rowley stated police are investigating whether an email from Mandelson to Epstein constitutes a criminal offence.

Democrats walked out of a House Oversight Committee briefing with Attorney General Pam Bondi regarding Epstein files; GOP Chairman James Comer characterized the walkout as premeditated, and Bondi stated she would 'follow the law' in response.
Wall Street titan Leon Black paid Jeffrey Epstein $170 million, which Black described as compensation for tax and estate work.
Leon Black paid Jeffrey Epstein $170 million, which Black described as payment for tax and estate work.
David A. Ross sought Jeffrey Epstein's help to build art museums and is now facing fallout related to that association.
Jeffrey Epstein's accountant Richard Khan and lawyer Darren Indyke testified before the House Oversight Committee, both stating the DOJ never interviewed them about Epstein's crimes.
Epstein survivors filed a class action lawsuit against the Trump administration and Google seeking at least $1,000 per survivor and court-ordered removal of their personal information by Google.
A man was interviewed on suspicion of sex trafficking in connection with the Al Fayed investigation, following earlier interviews with three women under caution.
Ramsey Elkholy introduced Jeffrey Epstein to women as young as 18 years old over nearly a decade, with correspondence documented in emails between them.
Jeffrey Epstein provided funding to scientists, and the lack of legal or public scrutiny in science philanthropy allowed him to cultivate relationships with scientists.
Epstein files indicate a 15-year-old girl met then-Prince Andrew at Buckingham Palace. Mandelson attempted to get access to 10 Downing Street for Epstein's goddaughter.
Attorney General Pam Bondi was fired by President Trump on Thursday; her handling of Epstein files was a point of congressional interest.
The Epstein files were released containing accusations against rich and powerful people, but the DOJ made no additional arrests, with legal experts citing lack of evidence.
Todd Blanche assumed the role of Interim Attorney General on Thursday, replacing Pam Bondi, and stated he wants to distance the Department of Justice from its work on Epstein files.

Virginia Giuffre, prior to her death, accused Jeffrey Epstein of trafficking her to Prince Andrew, brother of King Charles. The Giuffre family is urging King Charles to meet with Epstein survivors in the United States.
Jeffrey Epstein spent his final days of freedom in Paris, where he met with influential figures.
According to an FBI interview, Epstein had sex in a vehicle in a prison parking lot while on work release from a Florida jail approximately 20 years ago.

Bill Gates has agreed to appear before the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform in June as part of its investigation into deceased sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick is also scheduled to testify before the same House panel as part of the Epstein probe.

Attorney General Pam Bondi did not appear for a House Oversight Committee deposition subpoenaed in connection with its investigation into the Jeffrey Epstein files. The DOJ communicated that Bondi would not appear and informed the committee that its subpoena is essentially moot, though committee members maintain the subpoena remains valid.

The Department of Justice announced that Attorney General Pam Bondi would not testify before the House Oversight Committee, at least temporarily, despite having been subpoenaed as part of the committee's probe into the Jeffrey Epstein files. Separately, UK politician Peter Mandelson was reported to have attempted to obtain access to 10 Downing Street for a person described as Epstein's 'goddaughter.'

Melania Trump delivered a televised statement from the White House denying any connection to Jeffrey Epstein, stating 'I have never had any knowledge of Epstein's abuse of his victims,' 'I was never involved in any capacity,' 'I've never been friends with Epstein,' and 'I am not Epstein's victim.' She called on Congress to continue the investigation and hold hearings focused on Epstein's survivors, and declared that claims linking her to Epstein 'need to end today.'

On April 9, 2026, Melania Trump issued a rare public statement denying that Jeffrey Epstein introduced her to Donald Trump and calling on Congress to hold a hearing for Epstein survivors. Former Justice Department chief Pam Bondi refused to appear before a congressional Epstein hearing, with a subpoena for her testimony remaining in effect and Democrats criticizing her absence. Rep. Thomas Massie argued that bringing survivors back before Congress would be redundant and that the duty to act rests with federal prosecutors.

Melania Trump issued a rare public statement on Thursday denying any ties to Jeffrey Epstein, calling him 'disgraceful.' The statement was described as unexpected given her typically low public profile, and her adviser spoke publicly about what motivated her to issue it.

Melania Trump made a surprise public statement calling for testimony from Jeffrey Epstein victims. House Oversight Committee Chairman James Comer, a Republican from Kentucky, responded to her statement and confirmed that congressional hearings featuring Epstein victims will take place. Separately, Epstein survivors pushed back on the call for public testimony. The House Oversight Committee has been investigating allegations of sex trafficking connected to Epstein, who was a convicted sex offender and is deceased.

A federal judge dismissed Donald Trump's defamation lawsuit against the Wall Street Journal, which had centered on the outlet's reporting about a letter allegedly connected to Jeffrey Epstein's 50th birthday. The judge ruled that Trump failed to sufficiently allege 'actual malice,' the legal standard required for public figures in defamation cases.

The Justice Department's Office of Inspector General announced a review of the DOJ's compliance with laws requiring the release of Epstein-related records, amid concerns that required documents have not been fully disclosed.

Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick appeared before the House Oversight Committee on Wednesday in connection with the Epstein investigation. Ahead of the hearing, Committee Chair James Comer told reporters that Lutnick was not '100% truthful' about visiting Epstein's island.

A federal judge ordered the release of a document purported to be a suicide note attributed to Jeffrey Epstein, with the unsealing occurring on a Wednesday following a request by The New York Times. The note's authenticity has not been fully verified. Lutnick's testimony before the House Oversight Committee was conducted as a closed-door session.

Former Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene claimed on CBS News that President Trump is targeting Republicans who voted to release Epstein files, citing Rep. Thomas Massie's primary defeat as an example. Separately, a trespasser who illegally accessed Epstein's private island Little St. James claimed he was hog-tied and held in a dungeon on the property.

British police issued a public appeal for witnesses on a Friday as part of an investigation into potential sexual misconduct offenses by former Prince Andrew, with the probe connected to Jeffrey Epstein. Newly released papers revealed Prince Andrew was coached on how to justify his qualifications for a UK trade ambassador role after lawmakers accused him of prioritizing his Epstein ties over British interests. Sarah Kellen, described as both an alleged survivor and recruiter for Epstein, testified in a closed-door session before lawmakers, reportedly naming three individuals tied to abuse. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick donated $5 million to House Republicans after agreeing to be interviewed by lawmakers about his relationship with Epstein, according to the New York Times.

FEC filings confirmed that Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick donated the $5 million to the Congressional Leadership Fund, a House Republican super PAC, on April 1, specifically ahead of his congressional testimony regarding his ties to Jeffrey Epstein.

A U.S. document repository described as a 'library' has been established in New York to house 3.5 million pages of Epstein-related documents, aimed at providing accountability for victims, according to Al Jazeera. Rep. Thomas Massie attributed his primary loss to Trump-backed challenger Ed Gallrein to his bipartisan advocacy, particularly his push to release the Epstein files.

Rep. Thomas Massie, despite losing his primary race after being targeted by President Trump, promised to expose additional names from the Epstein files before his term ends in approximately seven months.

Vice President JD Vance admitted on The Joe Rogan Experience that the Trump administration 'absolutely screwed up the comms of the Epstein files,' publicly blaming former Attorney General Pam Bondi. Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche acknowledged during his Senate confirmation hearing that 'mistakes' were made in the redaction of the Epstein files. Former Obama White House counsel Kathryn Ruemmler was questioned by the House Oversight Committee in a bipartisan hearing over emails revealing her friendly relationship with Epstein. The U.S. Justice Department refused New Mexico's request for Epstein-related files, with New Mexico stating the withheld records are critical to its ongoing criminal investigation into alleged abuse at Epstein's ranch.

New Mexico Attorney General Raúl Torrez accused acting U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche of stonewalling the state's active Epstein investigation, directly contradicting Blanche's Senate confirmation hearing pledge to pursue new leads. Blanche separately agreed to meet with Epstein survivors following a demand from Senator Thom Tillis.

Epstein victims met with acting Attorney General Todd Blanche on Thursday; reactions were divided, with some describing the meeting as a meaningful first step and others dismissing it as a political exercise tied to Blanche's Senate confirmation process.

The House Oversight Committee subpoenaed billionaire Leon Black for a second interview scheduled in September, focusing on his friendship with Epstein and a birthday book; Black had previously paid Epstein $158 million for tax advice. A woman identified only as 'Anya' gave the BBC a first-hand account describing Epstein's methods of luring and controlling young women he called 'assistants,' including accounts of threats and disfiguring surgery within what she characterized as a cult-like environment.
Epstein survivor Jess Michaels described leaving her meeting with acting Attorney General Todd Blanche as 'disappointed, disturbed and undaunted.'

Epstein survivor Jess Michaels stated on MSNBC that she and other survivors were 'gaslit' during their meeting with acting Attorney General Todd Blanche, saying Blanche repeatedly denied claims about the Department of Justice's handling of the case.

Rep. Jamie Raskin and House Judiciary Democrats sent a letter to top Trump administration officials arguing that emails from Jeffrey Epstein to world leaders indicate he should have registered as a foreign agent, citing messages purportedly showing Epstein sought to leverage his relationship with President Trump.

Democratic candidates James Talarico and Jon Ossoff are facing scrutiny over major donations received from billionaire Reid Hoffman, who has previously been linked to Jeffrey Epstein, according to Fox News.

Daniel Siad, a French model scout linked to Jeffrey Epstein and under investigation in France for allegedly helping Epstein traffic and abuse women, was found dead at his home in a north-west suburb of Paris on Monday. French prosecutors confirmed his death.

Jean-Luc Brunel, a modeling agent described as having introduced women to Jeffrey Epstein, was also found dead in France, according to the Washington Post. This follows the earlier reported death of Daniel Siad, another Epstein-linked figure found dead in Paris.

Additional details on Daniel Siad's death confirmed that his name appeared roughly 2,000 times in the Epstein files and that he was linked to a sex trafficking probe involving at least 24 alleged victims or witnesses.

The NY Times identified Karyna Shuliak, 37, as Jeffrey Epstein's girlfriend and likely primary heir to his estate, noting she has sought to avoid public attention since his death. The Times also published a summary of key findings on Epstein's case and its international dimensions involving money, power, and complicity among prominent figures.
Epstein survivor Dani Bensky visited Capitol Hill to lobby senators against confirming Todd Blanche as attorney general, calling him 'walking perjury' in a CBS News interview.

UK Victims Minister Alex Davies-Jones told BBC Newsnight that Greater Manchester Mayor Andy Burnham is considering conducting a public inquiry into Jeffrey Epstein's actions in the United Kingdom, and that she had discussed the matter with the Prime Minister upon her appointment.
CBS News is facing renewed scrutiny over an unbroadcast '60 Minutes' segment on Jeffrey Epstein, following the release of a Senate Finance Committee report examining Epstein's banking connections.

New Mexico Attorney General Raúl Torrez filed a lawsuit against the Trump administration's DOJ seeking access to Jeffrey Epstein's files, citing an ongoing investigation into Epstein's Zorro Ranch property in New Mexico. The legal action coincides with Todd Blanche's approaching confirmation proceedings as attorney general.

A new report revealed approximately 70 allegations of sexual abuse involving nearly 50 adults employed or affiliated with Interlochen arts school, where Jeffrey Epstein allegedly preyed on students, according to accounts from former students.

A federal judge expressed frustration with DOJ attorneys over their handling of Epstein files, warning he has held attorneys in contempt before while stating he had 'absolutely no desire' to do so in this case. Trump's DOJ has been accused of noncompliance following a court hearing over missing documents and disclosures in the Epstein records lawsuit, according to Newsweek.
The DOJ signaled its intent to appeal a preliminary injunction requiring removal of redactions from key Epstein documents, in a lawsuit brought by attorney and independent journalist Katie Phang.

U.S. District Judge Paul Engelmayer denied Ghislaine Maxwell's habeas corpus petition, characterizing her claims as false and 'frivolous,' rejecting her bid to overturn her 2021 sex-trafficking conviction. Maxwell, who represented herself in the petition, had received a 20-year prison sentence for her role aiding Jeffrey Epstein.

Rep. Maxwell Frost (D-Fla.) stated that former President Biden and his administration should have released federal documents connected to Jeffrey Epstein, making the remarks during an appearance on Jubilee's 'Surrounded.'

The US and Iran are holding nuclear talks in Geneva aimed at resolving their nuclear dispute, with President Trump accompanying diplomatic efforts with military threats and a Middle East force buildup.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated progress has been made in negotiations with Iran after the U.S. sent a draft peace proposal to Tehran.
Following US-Israeli attacks on key infrastructure, Iranian hardliners and politicians are demanding withdrawal from the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty.
Iranian President Pezeshkian released a letter to Americans on X hours before Trump's scheduled address on Iran operations.
Iran rejected a U.S. ceasefire deal and instead conveyed a 10-point counterproposal through Pakistani intermediaries. The proposal demanded an end to ongoing attacks and an end to sanctions.

Pakistan has been mediating backchannel talks between the United States and Iran, with U.S. Vice President JD Vance involved in the mediation efforts. Iran has sought indirect engagement through the U.S. vice president.
Iran's ambassador to Pakistan stated that an Iranian delegation is scheduled to arrive in Islamabad on Thursday.
Negotiations between the U.S. and Iran are being hosted in Islamabad as both sides seek a diplomatic off-ramp to the conflict.

High-stakes U.S.-Iran negotiations were set for Islamabad this weekend, with Vice President JD Vance leading the American delegation in talks aimed at ending the war and finalizing ceasefire terms. The White House described the talks as ongoing, while Iranian Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei stated through state TV that Iran does not want war and seeks compensation. Some Republicans in Congress moved to assert legislative authority over any lasting deal with Tehran, citing a 2015 Obama-era law. China's role in the negotiations was also under discussion, with NBC News correspondent Janis Mackey Frayer covering that dimension of the diplomacy.

Vice President JD Vance traveled to Islamabad, Pakistan, to lead U.S. talks with Iranian officials aimed at ending the ongoing conflict, stating he expects 'positive' negotiations and that President Trump provided 'pretty clear guidelines' for the discussions. Iran's Parliament Speaker Mohammad-Bagher Ghalibaf posted on X that Iran will not negotiate with the U.S. without a ceasefire in Lebanon and the release of blocked Iranian assets, adding that two mutually agreed-upon measures have yet to be implemented. A fragile ceasefire remains in place, though multiple hurdles continue to strain it.

US and Iranian delegations convened in Islamabad, Pakistan, for high-stakes nuclear and diplomatic talks, with Pakistan serving as host and mediator. Vice President JD Vance participated on the US side, and a US plane carrying the American team was confirmed to have landed in Islamabad by two Pakistani sources. A fragile ceasefire between the US and Iran is currently in place, with the Strait of Hormuz among the key issues under negotiation.

Vice President JD Vance traveled to Islamabad, Pakistan on Saturday for direct talks with Iranian officials, the first such direct U.S.-Iran negotiations since 1979. The White House confirmed the talks, with Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif playing a mediating role in hosting the negotiations. A two-week ceasefire between the U.S. and Iran, described as fragile, remains in effect, and Iran is seeking sanctions relief as part of the discussions. Special envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner participated in trilateral talks with Iranian officials, drawing criticism from Sen. Mark Kelly. The Strait of Hormuz remains a key factor in the negotiations. Separately, Saudi Arabia confirmed that Pakistan sent fighter jets to the kingdom under a mutual defense pact.
After approximately 21 hours of negotiations in Pakistan, Vice President JD Vance announced that no deal was reached between the U.S. and Iran, describing the outcome as 'bad news for Iran.'

Trump initially told CNBC he did not want to extend the ceasefire with Iran, but ultimately announced an extension before the deadline expired. The extension is conditional, remaining in effect until Iran submits a proposal and discussions are concluded, while the blockade against Iran stays in place.

Iran submitted a response to a U.S. peace proposal aimed at ending the war, according to Iranian state media outlet IRNA. No details of Iran's response or the contents of the U.S. proposal have been publicly disclosed.

Trump claimed in a Fox News interview with Sean Hannity that during his talks with Xi Jinping in Beijing, Xi offered to help with Iran, specifically related to keeping the Strait of Hormuz open. Trump also stated that Xi committed to not providing military equipment to Iran, describing the pledge as significant.

Trump stated that the United States will retrieve uranium from Iran, reflecting tensions over its enrichment activities. Iranian Supreme Leader Khamenei has ordered that enriched uranium remain inside Iran rather than be transferred elsewhere. The U.S. Senate advanced a bill aimed at ending the war with Iran, with Senator Cassidy switching his position to support the measure after losing a primary election.

Trump announced via Truth Social on Saturday that a deal with Iran is 'largely negotiated,' stating that 'Final aspects and details of the Deal are currently being discussed, and will be announced shortly,' following a phone call with Gulf and regional Arab leaders to review Iran's latest proposal. The proposed deal would include reopening the Strait of Hormuz and formally ending the war between the U.S. and Iran. Secretary of State Marco Rubio separately stated that 'significant progress' has been made in negotiations. However, Iran and Iranian state media dismissed Trump's characterization as inconsistent with reality, and a senior Iranian source told Reuters that Iran has not agreed to hand over its highly enriched uranium stockpile, contradicting U.S. officials cited by the NY Times who said Iran had agreed to relinquish enriched uranium. Republican war hawks urged Trump to abandon peace efforts, and Senator Lindsey Graham raised concerns about the potential agreement, while details of what has formally been agreed upon remain unclear.
The White House dismissed an outline of an 'unofficial' Iran deal, according to the NY Times.

Israel believes Iran moved nuclear material and centrifuges into the heavily fortified underground site known as Pickaxe Mountain, located near the Natanz nuclear facility, in an apparent effort to protect or conceal nuclear enrichment equipment from further strikes.
U.S. intelligence agencies assess that Iran's new supreme leader is more open to pursuing a nuclear weapon than his predecessor, who had renounced such weapons before being killed early in the war.

The U.S.-Iran memorandum of understanding signed on June 17 began unraveling less than a month later, with the U.S. relaunching full-scale strikes on Iranian targets on July 11, according to the Washington Examiner.
Officials and experts assessed that the conflict has slowed but not stopped Iran's nuclear program, with its three key nuclear sites remaining operational, according to the NY Times.
Vice President JD Vance claimed the United States has 'destroyed' Iran's nuclear programme and degraded its military capabilities, according to Al Jazeera.

A false claim that Iran had declared itself a nuclear power originated from a dubious post on X and spread from India to Washington, with the New York Times tracing how the misinformation ricocheted across platforms and into public discourse.
Russia launched drone and missile strikes on Ukrainian cities and infrastructure near the time of scheduled US-Ukraine talks in Geneva.
A Russian-operated gas tanker sank in the Mediterranean Sea following a Ukrainian drone attack, which Russia attributed to Ukraine.
A Russian-flagged gas tanker sank in the Mediterranean Sea following a drone attack that Russia attributed to Ukraine.
Russian publication Izvestia reported that Ukraine peace talks have been paused in connection with the Iran war.
Ukraine reported hitting a Russian oil terminal at Primorsk and a refinery in Ufa on Monday.
Zelenskyy stated that Ukraine has evidence that Russia is supplying Iran with intelligence.
Russia launched a large drone attack on Ukrainian cities including Lviv, damaging a UNESCO World Heritage site and injuring multiple people.
Ukrainian President Zelenskiy stated that the US has linked security guarantees to Ukraine ceding Donbas territory.
Ukrainian President Zelenskiy stated that the US has linked security guarantees to Ukraine giving up Donbas, according to Reuters.
Zelensky visited Saudi Arabia and offered Ukraine's drone expertise.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky made a surprise visit to Saudi Arabia to offer Ukraine's drone defense expertise developed during the war against Russia to the U.S. and Gulf States.
Russia announced a ban on gasoline exports starting April 1.
Russian strikes on Ukraine killed 4 people, and US Secretary of State Marco Rubio expressed openness to diverting weapons to Kyiv.
Ukrainian drones damaged Russia's Ust-Luga port, causing a fire to break out.
President Zelenskyy stated in an NBC News interview that he hopes President Trump cares about Ukraine's future, noting that Trump administration priorities center on the United States.
Ukraine's president stated that allies asked him about reducing attacks on Russian energy as prices rise due to the Iran war.
Estonia's defence forces detected an air threat overnight.
Ukraine's president hosted EU leaders at an event marking the Bucha massacre anniversary while Ukraine's negotiator Umerov was in Turkey for talks.
A Russian military transport plane crashed in Crimea, killing 29 people, according to the Russian Defense Ministry.
A Russian military transport plane crashed in Crimea, killing 29 people. Officials cited possible technical malfunction.
Russia is recruiting students for its drone forces in Ukraine and offering large financial packages as part of recruitment efforts.
Ukrainian President Zelensky warned about Russia's intelligence sharing with Iran in an exclusive NewsNation interview and discussed Ukraine's assistance to the US in its conflict with Iran.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky warned in an exclusive interview about Russia's intelligence sharing with Iran and discussed how Ukraine is helping the US in its war against Iran.
Fuel leaks occurred at Russia's Primorsk oil facility and a fire broke out at the NORSI oil refinery in Nizhny Novgorod, according to Russian authorities.
Zelenskiy traveled to Syria and met with President Sharaa.
A child was rescued from rubble after a Russian strike collapsed a home in Odesa, killing at least three people.
The Iran war has driven shortages and price spikes across multiple consumer product categories beyond oil and gas, including beer cans, helium balloons, and mortgages.

Farmers warned that the Iran war and its associated costs would drive up their expenses and subsequently affect food prices, with the recently announced ceasefire not expected to immediately relieve those pressures.

Vladimir Putin announced a ceasefire coinciding with Orthodox Easter weekend, including April 12, and both Russia and Ukraine signaled agreement to the truce. President Zelensky stated that Ukraine will complete repairs to the Druzhba oil pipeline in spring and said peace talks to end the war could resume soon, though he expressed skepticism about any imminent breakthrough.

A 32-hour Easter truce was established between Ukraine and Russia, though both Ukrainians and Russians expressed doubt it would lead to lasting peace. Russian casualties are mounting, recruitment is falling, and territorial gains are dwindling, while Ukraine has been increasing drone production. President Zelensky traveled to the Middle East in March, securing a series of 10-year agreements with Gulf State leaders, and subsequently announced that Ukrainian interceptors had downed Iranian drones in the region, with 228 Ukrainian experts previously deployed there.

Russian drone strikes killed at least two people in the Ukrainian city of Odesa overnight into Saturday, according to local authorities. A Ukrainian drone attack in Russia's Kursk region injured three people, as reported by the regional governor. Separately, Ukraine and Russia exchanged 175 servicemen each ahead of an Easter ceasefire.
Russia launched one of the most intense aerial attacks of the year on Ukraine, sending hundreds of drones and missiles overnight in a hours-long assault targeting civilian areas across the country.
Vladimir Putin declared his belief that the war with Ukraine is 'coming to an end' as a new three-day ceasefire went into effect.
Ukraine launched one of its largest drone attacks on Russia, killing at least four people, three of them in the Moscow region.

Russia conducted joint military exercises with Belarus that included delivering nuclear warheads to Belarusian sites, with the drills described as rehearsals for the use of nuclear forces. Ukraine conducted attacks targeting Russian energy infrastructure sites as part of ongoing military operations.

Russia condemned a Ukrainian strike on occupied Luhansk as a 'monstrous crime,' claiming a student dormitory was hit and at least four people killed. Ukrainian officials reported Russia has suffered approximately 83,000 soldiers killed so far in 2026 and is actively seeking to recruit new soldiers, with independent estimates also suggesting Russia's economy is faltering.
Putin vowed retaliation following the Luhansk strike, while Ukraine stated the attack targeted Russia's elite Rubicon drone military unit operating in Moscow-occupied eastern Ukraine.

The drone strike on a student dormitory in Russian-controlled Luhansk was reported to have killed 16 people, with most victims described as young women, adding detail to previously reported Russian accusations. Ukraine claimed it struck Russia's Sheskharis oil terminal on the Black Sea. Ukrainian President Zelenskyy warned that Russia is preparing to strike Ukraine using a hypersonic 'Oreshnik' missile.

Russia launched a massive missile and drone attack on Kyiv overnight, killing at least four people and injuring more than 50, including three children, with damage reported at 40 locations across the capital and nearby areas. Ukrainian President Zelenskyy stated the attack included Russia's hypersonic Oreshnik ballistic missile, which Russia confirmed it deployed using hypersonic and ballistic missiles, though the NY Times reported it remained unclear whether the Oreshnik was used. Prior to the attack, Zelenskyy had warned on social media that Ukraine was bracing for a 'significant air attack' involving hypersonic missiles and stated Ukraine was working to verify U.S. and allied intelligence on Russia's Oreshnik deployment plans.

Russia's Oreshnik ballistic missile strike on Ukraine — its third such use since the war began — was confirmed by Ukrainian President Zelenskyy as part of Sunday's barrage on Kyiv, which killed four people and injured approximately 100, with damage reported to 30 residential buildings.

European leaders condemned Russia's hypersonic ballistic missile strike on Kyiv. Energy infrastructure was also damaged in a separate missile attack on Russia's Belgorod region, according to local authorities cited by Reuters.

The EU is actively searching for potential mediators to help broker an end to the war in Ukraine following U.S. withdrawal from trilateral talks, according to BBC News. Ukraine used British-supplied Storm Shadow missiles in an attack on Sevastopol, according to the city's governor. The GCHQ Director is set to deliver a speech Wednesday warning that Russia is 'relentlessly targeting' critical infrastructure and democracy, outlining threats facing the UK and proposed countermeasures. UN Secretary-General Guterres expressed being 'deeply concerned' following Russia's announcement of plans to strike Kyiv.
GCHQ Director Anne Keast-Butler, in her first public speech, stated that almost 500,000 Russian soldiers have been killed in the Ukraine war.

Ukrainian President Zelensky appealed directly to Trump and members of Congress on Wednesday, requesting Patriot missile interceptors and citing Ukraine's lack of domestic capability to produce anti-missile defense systems. The U.S. Embassy in Kyiv denied reports of an evacuation, disputing claims by EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas that Washington had withdrawn personnel amid escalating Russian airstrike threats. Ukrainian veterans returning from the front are facing a growing mental health crisis, according to a Washington Examiner report from Lviv.

Ukrainian Prime Minister Yulia Svyrydenko resigned on Sunday as President Zelensky reshuffled his cabinet, citing the need for 'personnel changes' to implement an 'updated political strategy.' Allied nations are mobilizing additional air defense assistance for Ukraine amid shifting battlefield momentum, according to Reuters. Ground robots in Ukraine have transitioned from logistical roles to active combat functions including trench holding, casualty evacuation, and offensive operations, marking a significant shift in modern ground warfare, according to the NY Times.

Western leaders reached an agreement to form an anti-ballistic missile coalition with Ukraine, according to Reuters. President Zelensky stated that outgoing Prime Minister Svyrydenko was offered a new role focused on relations with a key international partner as part of the government reshuffle.

Nine European countries and Ukraine launched a coalition to develop Europe's own ballistic missile defence shield, according to Al Jazeera. France displayed 500 pro-Ukraine troops during its Bastille Day celebrations.

Ukraine has shifted its military campaign to target Russian ships in order to disrupt sea routes to Crimea, following earlier strikes on roads and railways, with the effort aimed at cutting off fuel supplies to Russian forces and increasing pressure on Moscow to end the war.

Ukrainian drones struck 20 vessels in the Sea of Azov as part of a new naval campaign targeting Russian shipping. Ukraine's farmers' union reported that the country's Black Sea ports have lost a third of their grain export capacity. Russia declared that any foreign troops deployed to Ukraine following a peace deal would be considered legitimate military targets. EU envoys failed to reach agreement on a 21st package of sanctions against Russia.

Mykhailo Fedorov departed from his role as Ukraine's Defense Minister, triggering mass protests across Ukrainian cities. Russian missiles struck Kyiv, with Mayor Vitali Klitschko reporting emergency services battling fires across the capital following the EU and Ukraine signing a drone deal. Ukraine launched at least 200 drones toward Moscow overnight into Thursday, according to Moscow Mayor Sergey Sobyanin. UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer traveled to Kyiv to meet President Zelensky, pledging the UK's 'cast-iron' support for Ukraine.

UK Prime Minister Starmer announced that the UK will help fund 16 Gripen fighter jets for Ukraine. Zelensky's dismissal of Defense Minister Fedorov was confirmed as part of a surprise government reshuffle, with Fedorov having been a popular figure known for championing drone innovation in battlefield tactics; rare protests erupted in Kyiv in response.
Ukrainian President Zelensky also dismissed Defense Minister Rustem Umerov, credited as a key architect of Ukraine's drone program, as part of the broader government reshuffle.

Ukraine cut off Crimea from Russia, triggering an energy crisis on the peninsula. Russian attacks on Ukrainian ports killed two Ukrainians aboard a foreign vessel in Mykolaiv, with two additional deaths reported in Kherson and Odesa.

Ukrainian drone strikes hit Wildberries online retail warehouses near Moscow and in Tambov, Russia, killing seven warehouse workers and igniting a fire at an oil depot in the Moscow region. President Zelensky described the targets as major logistics facilities supplying sanctioned components to Russia.

Ukrainian drone attacks killed at least eight people inside Russia and wounded dozens more, with strikes targeting energy infrastructure and military sites in addition to the logistics facilities previously reported. Al Jazeera separately reported a Ukrainian strike on a Russian logistics center, with no additional details on location or scale provided.

Russia launched a large-scale overnight attack on Ukraine on Sunday, firing 41 ballistic missiles and 125 drones, with strikes hitting Kyiv and the surrounding region. At least one person was killed and nine wounded in the Kyiv attack. Separately, the New York Times reported that Ukraine's overnight strikes on two warehouses inside Russia killed at least eight people and injured 62. BBC News reported that Russians are increasingly turning to cash transactions amid mobile internet shutdowns, with businesses seeking to avoid taxes as Russia's wartime economy shows signs of slowing after more than four years of conflict.

Kyiv was struck in the largest ballistic missile attack of the war, with over 50 missiles fired including 38 Iskander ballistic missiles and six Zircon hypersonic cruise missiles; few were intercepted due to Ukraine's depleted interceptor stockpiles.

Ukraine launched approximately 400 drones targeting the Moscow region, according to Russian authorities cited by Reuters, resulting in two people wounded and several buildings set ablaze. Separately, BBC News reported that aggression against military recruitment officers in Ukraine has become increasingly threatening as the country's struggle to recruit soldiers intensifies.

A Russian strike on a ship near Odesa killed 10 people, with India's government confirming four of the dead were Indian nationals. Zelensky faces mounting pressure from protesters and soldiers to remove Ukraine's top general, with demonstrators also calling for reaffirmation of a drone warfare strategy associated with the recently dismissed defense minister.

Ukraine conducted bombing strikes targeting Wildberries warehouses, the large Russian e-commerce platform. Protests are growing in Ukraine over President Zelensky's decision to fire the country's defense minister, with Zelensky's office signaling openness to compromise in response to public pressure. Defense companies are developing faster jet-powered interceptor drones to counter Russia's deployment of higher-speed Shahed drones in Ukraine.

Zelensky dismissed Ukraine's top army commander, Gen. Oleksandr Syrskyi, following protests demanding his removal and the reinstatement of former Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov, with demonstrators having set a Friday deadline for their demands.

Maj. Gen. Mykhailo Drapatyi was appointed as Ukraine's new commander-in-chief, replacing Syrskyi; the NY Times described him as a decorated commander with popularity both domestically and internationally. The Wildberries strikes targeted logistics hubs specifically in the Krasnodar and Stavropol regions, and Ukraine had previously struck the company's facilities in an earlier attack. Outgoing Gen. Syrskyi stated that Ukraine recaptured 700 square kilometers of territory in the current year. The House of Representatives voted 76-350 to reject an amendment to the NDAA that would have blocked Pentagon funding for Ukraine security assistance. A Reuters report highlighted the account of a Ukrainian soldier who survived approximately one year living in a foxhole beneath the front lines.

Greece is resisting proposed sanctions on Russian LNG shipping, warning of significant impacts on its shipping industry, while simultaneously expressing concern over Russian hybrid warfare threats. Ukraine agreed to export drones to the United States as part of a Pentagon plan, according to a Reuters source. Mykhailo Drapatyi, now Ukraine's third commander-in-chief since Russia's full-scale invasion began in February 2022, faces the challenge of transitioning from battlefield command to broader bureaucratic leadership responsibilities. Zelenskyy stated that the Wildberries warehouses struck by Ukrainian drones were 'involved in supplying the Russian army' with military equipment including body armor and drone parts.
A Ukrainian attack on Crimea killed one person and injured four others, according to Russian authorities.

Ukraine shot down a Russian Su-35 fighter jet using an F-16, marking the first recorded air-to-air kill by a Western-supplied fighter in the conflict. At least four people were killed in Russian strikes on Ukraine, while four others died in Russia and Crimea as both sides exchanged deep strikes. Secretary of State Marco Rubio held discussions with Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov regarding the war.

A Russian ballistic missile strike on a drone exhibition near Kyiv killed ten people, with the event attended by prominent members of Ukraine's defense industry. Separately, a Ukrainian drone strike destroyed a Russian Tu-95MS strategic bomber, according to satellite imagery reported by Newsweek, and at least six people were killed in a Ukrainian strike on Russia's Kirov region. Russia has withdrawn all warships from the Mediterranean Sea, a move attributed to losses and sustained pressure on its Black Sea Fleet from Ukrainian drone strikes. Ukrainian President Zelensky met with Raytheon to discuss co-production of Patriot missile interceptors following Trump's approval for Ukraine-U.S. cooperation on their manufacturing.

Protests continued in Ukraine over President Zelensky's dismissal of Defence Minister Rustem Fedorov, with commentators suggesting Zelensky has been politically damaged by the decision. Italy's Defence Minister offered Fedorov an adviser role, according to Reuters.

Ukrainian attacks on holiday camps in the partly Russian-occupied Zaporizhzhia region killed at least 11 people, with Russia claiming responsibility for the civilian death toll framing, according to multiple outlets. A drone threat in Yekaterinburg disrupted operations at online retailer Wildberries and caused interruptions to an athletics championships event. President Zelensky stated Russia intends to deploy 30,000 additional North Korean troops to the conflict, and announced a joint U.S.-Ukraine drone factory will be built in the United States. Iran announced that a Ukrainian attack on a vessel in the Caspian Sea killed a sailor, according to Reuters.

Ukraine struck a Wildberries logistics hub in Russia, described as the seventh attack on the e-commerce chain suspected of supplying Moscow's military, setting vehicles ablaze and prompting employee evacuations.

Laura Loomer publicly reversed her position on the Ukraine war after visiting the country, stating she had been wrong about U.S. military aid to Ukraine. Iran vowed revenge following the Ukrainian drone attack on an Iranian commercial vessel in the Caspian Sea that killed at least one sailor, with Iran's Foreign Minister warning the attack 'cannot go unanswered'; Ukrainian President Zelensky confirmed the strikes, saying Ukraine had achieved 'very strong results.'

A Ukrainian drone strike on the Russian border city of Belgorod wounded 12 people, according to local authorities. Russia and Ukraine exchanged strikes, with Kyiv reporting six killed — including a child at a supermarket in Chernihiv — while Moscow reported four killed in Ukrainian strikes. Ukraine is also seeking a prototype of a European missile defence system by mid-2027, according to a Ukrainian official cited by Reuters.

Ukraine dismissed Iranian threats following Tehran's vow that the Caspian Sea vessel strike 'cannot go unanswered.' According to Newsmax, Russia is moving toward a 'real war' footing with plans for mobilization and escalation expected to follow the Duma elections.

Ukrainian President Zelensky is set to meet President Trump at the White House, according to the NY Times, and will also attend the funeral of Senator Lindsey Graham in Washington. Zelensky is additionally scheduled to meet with U.S. senators as the Senate prepares to vote on Russian sanctions. Separately, Zelensky met with Britain's new leader to discuss drone projects and missile defense systems for Kyiv.

Moscow issued a threat after Romania intercepted a series of Russian drones, following repeated drone incursions near the Danube River as Russia continues to bombard Ukrainian ports in the region. NATO's top transformation commander warned that the West cannot produce Patriot missiles fast enough to meet demand, stating 'the math is not in favor of the West' and calling for a full redesign of NATO's weapons industrial base.

The U.S. Senate advanced a bipartisan sanctions bill targeting Russian oil and gas exports, which also includes penalties against Iran and tariffs of up to 500% on Russian energy, with 100% tariffs applicable to buyers such as China.
Ukrainian President Zelensky warned that Russia is preparing a military draft that could mobilize up to 500,000 new soldiers, a development he said could significantly shape the course of the war.

Russia launched ballistic missile strikes on Kyiv following Zelensky's return from Washington, killing at least eight civilians including two girls aged 5 and 12 near Kryvyi Rih, with additional fatalities in Kyiv and Poltava and dozens wounded. Zelensky attributed the deaths to 'insufficient or delayed' air defense supplies, as Kyiv reported a shortage of Western-supplied anti-ballistic missile defenses. The U.S. Senate advanced a sanctions package allowing up to 500% tariffs on Russian imports and 100% tariffs on countries purchasing Russian energy, including China and India.

Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk confirmed a Russian missile struck Polish territory during a large-scale Russian attack involving an estimated 83 missiles targeting Kyiv, Kryvyi Rih, and Lviv, though no injuries were reported in Poland — with Poland scrambling fighter jets after the Kh-101 missile entered NATO airspace. Reuters reported that Russia likely used a North Korean ballistic missile in a deadly strike on Ukraine for the first time this year. Kazakhstan's oil export route through the Black Sea was shut down again after Ukrainian drone attacks targeted the Black Sea export gateway, per Reuters. Reuters also reported that gaps in civilian shelter availability are leaving Ukrainians desperate as Russian strikes continue to mount.

Russian forces have reportedly infiltrated most of Kostiantynivka as Moscow attempts to regain offensive momentum in eastern Ukraine. Ukraine struck Russian oil refineries multiple times while Russia attacked Dnipropetrovsk and hit a cargo vessel near Odesa. Russia's grain lobby warned that Ukrainian strikes in the Black Sea region threaten Russian grain exports and global food security. President Trump walked back his earlier support for providing Patriot missile systems to Ukraine, stating he is 'not sure' about the matter. Ukraine separately offered the Pentagon access to test its battlefield drones at reduced cost, though Kyiv indicated it cannot transfer associated technological secrets without compensation.

Trump backed away from a deal that would have allowed Ukraine to manufacture Patriot missile interceptors domestically, despite Zelensky's warnings that Ukraine is running low on the munitions. The Lithuanian embassy in Kyiv was damaged in a Russian missile attack. Thousands of protesters gathered on Kyiv's main street calling for the return of a defence minister. Ukraine and its supporters have been working to counter skepticism about the war effort within Trump's MAGA movement, including outreach toward Trump ally Laura Loomer.

A Russian overnight ballistic missile barrage struck five districts of Kyiv, killing nine people. A Rosatom civilian vessel sank in the Black Sea following a Ukrainian drone attack, with all crew members surviving. Ukrainian strikes on power infrastructure in Crimea disrupted electricity services, with families seen queuing for hot meals. Zelensky reportedly asked Trump in a closed-door Oval Office meeting to help persuade Elon Musk to expand Starlink access to enable its use in Ukrainian drone strikes against Russia.

Ukrainian drone attacks on Moscow in early 2026 have already surpassed the total number of such strikes recorded throughout all of 2025, according to Newsweek, marking a significant escalation in Ukraine's long-range drone campaign. Separately, Ukrainian drone strikes killed two people in Russia and hit a Wildberries warehouse, per Reuters.

Russia's military reported overnight attacks on Ukraine's Black Sea ports and vessels, while Ukraine claimed strikes on a major Russian oil refinery and airfield, with Moscow reporting eight deaths. Ukrainian drone strikes killed five people in Russia and set fire to a Wildberries warehouse, according to AP News. The crew of an Iranian ship struck in a Ukrainian attack has returned home, according to an Iranian news agency cited by Reuters.

Ukrainian President Zelenskyy is pushing partner nations to provide 300 Patriot interceptors for Ukraine's air defense, while a former Ukrainian official has described 'scandalous situations' amid a deepening probe into the country's bomb shelters. Russian aircraft dropped eight glide bombs on a city in southern Ukraine, killing one person and wounding dozens, according to regional chief Ivan Fedorov. Wildberries confirmed that one of its warehouses in the Vladimir region was set on fire following a Ukrainian drone attack.

A Ukrainian drone struck a crowded beach near the Black Sea resort of Gelendzhik, with Russia attributing the attack to Ukraine; approximately 40 people were injured and three children were among those killed. Ukraine conducted another long-range drone strike on a Wildberries warehouse, marking at least the second attack on the Russian e-commerce company's facilities. Ukraine's top negotiator Rustem Umerov was appointed to head the country's foreign intelligence service, according to Reuters. Al Jazeera reported that Russia and Ukraine exchanged heavy attacks killing more than 10 people as the conflict enters its fifth year.

Ukrainian strikes on warehouses across Russia killed five people according to local officials, with facilities in the Moscow region among those hit. Separately, a Russian soldier in Crimea killed one fellow soldier and three civilians.

Video footage showed a Russian drone pursuing a civilian street vendor at an outdoor produce market in Ukraine, prompting Kyiv to accuse Russia of committing a war crime. A separate drone strike on Gelendzhik beach killed seven beachgoers, with Russia and Ukraine trading blame over responsibility, updating earlier reports of the incident. Russian drones have struck hundreds of gas stations across Ukraine in what the NY Times describes as apparent retaliation for Ukrainian attacks on Russian oil refineries. Nine people were killed overall in escalating long-range missile and drone exchanges hitting targets well beyond the front lines. Ukraine has shifted to alternative grain export routes after Russia blocked its ports, with officials reporting significant agricultural export losses.

Russian missile and drone strikes targeted Kyiv and the surrounding region overnight into Wednesday, killing at least 15 people according to Ukraine's state emergency service, with President Zelenskyy confirming the casualty figures. Ukraine is reported to be running critically low on interceptor missiles needed to defend against Russian bombardments, underscoring Zelenskyy's push for more Patriot interceptors from partners. Zelenskyy also announced that Ukrainian drones killed or gravely wounded 30,272 Russian troops near the front lines in July. The US is continuing negotiations over supplying Patriot missile systems to Ukraine despite reported doubts from President Trump about the plan, according to Reuters sources.

Russia's overnight strike on Kyiv killed 17 people, with Russian officials claiming the attacks targeted logistics and transport infrastructure using precision weapons, updating earlier casualty figures. Newsweek reported that Russian forces have been conducting so-called 'drone safaris' hunting Ukrainian personnel near the front lines.

A Ukrainian intelligence official reported that Russia is deploying a North Korean unit equipped with up to 120 ballistic missiles to Ukraine, deepening the military axis between Moscow and Pyongyang. Russian strikes killed six people in Balakliia and Sumy, according to Ukrainian officials cited by Reuters. Russia has also intensified strikes on Ukraine's Black Sea coastline, with BBC News reporting visible damage to ships and docks in Odesa. Western allies are increasingly reluctant to supply Ukraine with additional air defense interceptors, citing concerns about maintaining their own stockpiles amid conflicts on multiple fronts, according to the NY Times.

Ukraine launched overnight drone strikes on two major oil refineries deep inside Russian territory, with President Zelenskyy stating the attacks were aimed at limiting revenues Russia uses to finance its war effort.

Ukraine launched a long-range drone strike that set fire to a warehouse belonging to a Russian retail giant. Russia launched a record number of glide bombs against Ukraine, according to Al Jazeera, as Moscow's forces suffered high casualty rates. UN Secretary-General António Guterres condemned both sides and called for de-escalation and a ceasefire as attacks intensified.

The US Senate passed sweeping legislation imposing aggressive economic sanctions on Russia, including a 100 percent tariff on importers of Russian oil and gas. Russian missile attacks near Kyiv killed three people, including a child, according to BBC News, as President Zelensky warned of Ukraine's dwindling missile interceptor supplies. Ukrainian emergency workers warned of increasing Russian drone attacks targeting hospitals and ambulances, with medics reporting they fled to survive the strikes, according to BBC News.

A viral video showing Ukrainian military recruiters forcibly apprehending a civilian man sparked public outcry over alleged abusive recruitment practices, with critics coining the term 'busification' to describe the phenomenon. Ukrainian volunteer Oleksiy Yukov, known for spending two decades recovering fallen soldiers' bodies from conflict zones on both sides, was killed after stepping on a landmine during a recovery mission.

Ukraine denied responsibility after a drone exploded near a gas pipeline in Bulgaria, according to CBS News. Russia reported striking fuel storage facilities at Ukrainian ports overnight, and Russian authorities said three people were killed in a Ukrainian drone strike on Belgorod.

Overnight exchanges of strikes killed at least 7 civilians and injured dozens more, with a Russian missile striking a high-rise apartment building causing over a dozen injuries. President Zelenskyy announced Odesa port sustained damage in a Russian attack and separately stated that up to 50,000 North Korean troops are to be deployed in Russia. Pope Leo renewed his call for an end to the war, and Turkish officials stated that ship passage to the Black Sea is continuing smoothly.

A Ukrainian drone attack struck Nizhnekamsk, an industrial city in Russia's Tatarstan region, killing at least 12 people — making it one of the deadliest Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian territory since the war began. Separately, Draganfly CEO Cameron Chell told Fox News that drone company leaders have become primary assassination targets from both Russian and Ukrainian operatives as the two sides compete for AI and autonomous weapons advantages.

Russian authorities revised the Nizhnekamsk death toll upward to 13 killed and 75 wounded in the Ukrainian drone strike on the petroleum hub in Tatarstan. Ukraine cut its grain export forecast following Russian attacks on its seaports, according to Reuters. Al Jazeera was granted rare access to one of Ukraine's long-range drone units conducting strikes inside Russia. Kyiv also reported that Russia is deploying a Starlink-style satellite internet network at a faster pace than previously anticipated, with potential military implications for the conflict.
Al Jazeera's Audrey MacAlpine reported from a secret launch site in eastern Ukraine, where Ukrainian soldiers were shown preparing long-range drones for deep-strike missions inside Russia.

Russia is set to hold its first parliamentary elections since the start of the full-scale invasion of Ukraine more than four years ago. Russia's Sibur petrochemical plant in western Siberia was shut down following a drone attack, according to Reuters sources.

Ukraine halted strikes on tankers using a Russian port following a request from the United States, according to the Financial Times. Russia's Novorossiysk grain terminal suspended operations after a Ukrainian drone attack, according to an industry source cited by Reuters.

Ukrainian President Zelenskyy announced a nighttime strike damaged Russia's Black Sea naval stronghold, as reported by AP News. Ukrainian forces also attacked major Russian grain export terminals in a Black Sea port, according to BBC News. Zelenskyy separately announced Ukraine has retaken 745 square kilometers of territory through a 'precision' operation in 2025. Russia's economy faces mounting pressure from a widening budget deficit and Ukrainian infrastructure strikes, even as Middle East conflict has boosted its oil revenues, according to Al Jazeera.

Russia's blockade of major Ukrainian ports threatens global grain supplies, according to the NY Times. Nobel Peace Prize winner Dmitry Muratov told BBC News that Putin can no longer claim victory in Ukraine, stating he can only 'destroy Ukraine, not conquer it,' as the war enters its fifth year.

The UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission reported at least 437 civilians killed and 2,610 injured in Ukraine in July, the highest monthly civilian death toll since May 2022. A bomb killed a Russian military officer in Crimea, with reports identifying the victim as a defector from Ukraine, though details were not independently verified. Ukraine has intensified drone strikes on Crimea by both air and sea, disrupting daily life on the Russian-held peninsula.
Ukrainian drone strikes knocked out 27% of the warehouse capacity of Wildberries, the Russian e-commerce company often compared to Amazon, with estimated losses of up to $8.5 billion.

Ukraine claimed to have liberated 26 settlements in the south while facing intensified Russian ballistic missile attacks, with Kyiv also reporting advances in the Dnipropetrovsk region, according to Al Jazeera. Russia's Sheskharis oil terminal on the Black Sea halted loadings after a drone attack, according to sources cited by Reuters.

Ukraine announced it struck a Russian rocket centre linked to what it described as a Starlink-style satellite network, according to Reuters. Ukraine also struck targets in Russia's southwestern Samara region using domestically produced Flamingo missiles, according to Al Jazeera.

Ukraine launched one of its largest aerial attacks of the war, sending hundreds of drones across Russia on Sunday, killing at least six people. Russian strikes killed three people across Ukraine, with firefighters responding to a market fire in Kyiv. Ukrainian drones struck the Moscow region, killing one person. A NATO jet shot down a drone over Romanian territory, with Romania's Defence Ministry not specifying its origin. Ousted Ukrainian Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov, credited as the architect of Ukraine's modern war-fighting strategy, gave an exclusive interview to CBS News describing the conflict as a 'technological war.' A Ukrainian bank worker, his mother, and girlfriend face terrorism charges and a potential life sentence in Russia, with all three maintaining innocence.

UK-made drones were used for the first time to strike military and industrial targets inside mainland Russia, according to BBC News. Russia reported its largest Ukrainian drone attack to date, with 822 drones shot down across Russian territory. Six people were also injured in a strike on a second-hand market in Ukraine selling records, posters, toys, and tools, with BBC News visiting the smouldering site.

The EU's foreign policy chief announced plans for the most far-reaching sanctions package against Russia to date, to be introduced in autumn, according to Reuters. Ukrainian strikes on Russia's Belgorod region killed six people and injured five others, including a 14-year-old child, according to the region's acting governor.

Robert Shaheiev, the Ukrainian naval officer who defected and surrendered the submarine Zaporizhzhia to Russia during the 2014 annexation of Crimea, has reportedly been killed, according to Newsweek. Former Ukrainian Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov stated he believes Ukraine will launch its own ballistic missile strike into Russia before the end of the year.

Russia shot down over 600 drones targeting the Moscow region in a single overnight attack, injuring at least three people and damaging a Wildberries warehouse, according to Russian officials including Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin. Ukrainian forces also launched a broader strike of nearly 800 drones at Russian territory. Separately, a Russian missile strike killed 10 people and injured over a dozen in a residential village in Ukraine's Kharkiv region, prompting President Zelensky to vow retaliation and describe the attack as 'brutal.'

A drone exploded at a bus stop at the Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant, killing one person, according to the IAEA. Russian Foreign Minister Lavrov warned that Britain risks being seen as a co-belligerent in the war, following UK Prime Minister Burnham's reaffirmation that the UK will support Ukraine '100 percent.'

Croatian authorities arrested two Ukrainian nationals alleged to have been among the scuba divers who planted explosives on the Nord Stream pipelines in 2022, according to BBC News, Al Jazeera, and AP News. The arrests come roughly one year after a former Ukrainian army officer was detained and transferred to Germany in connection with the same incident. A suspected sabotage attack targeting Estonian defense firm Milrem Robotics failed to disrupt the company's deliveries to Ukraine, according to Reuters. Al Jazeera also reported that Ukraine's military conscription practice known as 'busification' — the forcible capture of men on the street for service — has escalated into violence, with accounts of abuse and corruption surrounding the process.

Russian ballistic missiles struck Kyiv, killing at least 3 people and wounding at least 20 more. The Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant lost its external power supply, according to Reuters, with no immediate details on cause or restoration. BBC News interviewed Ukrainian-born soldiers held at a POW camp in western Ukraine who said they believed they were defending their homeland by fighting for Russia; the men face treason charges under Ukrainian law. Global wheat buyers are preparing for a potential supply squeeze as attacks in the Black Sea region threaten grain shipments, raising concerns over international availability and pricing.

Russia launched an additional massive attack on Ukraine involving dozens of missiles and more than 100 drones, with strikes hitting parts of Kyiv and killing 12 people while sparking fires, according to Newsmax and CBS News. Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping jointly declared the U.S.'s proposed Golden Dome missile shield a 'threat to strategic stability,' warning against what they characterized as a new arms race. Latvia confirmed that a drone that entered its airspace on August 14 belonged to Ukraine.
A Russian drone attack on Kyiv overnight Wednesday into Thursday killed at least 16 people and wounded 40 more, according to CBS News.

Russian drivers are facing hours-long queues at fuel stations amid petrol shortages, according to BBC News. The Nord Stream pipeline suspect arrest previously reported involves a Ukrainian national detained in Croatia, confirmed separately by Reuters.

A Russian drone strike hit a shopping mall in Kryvyi Rih — the hometown of President Zelenskyy — killing at least 16 people in a double-tap, two-wave attack. Russian strikes on Ukraine the following day killed at least two more people. In overnight strikes, Ukrainian drones hit a warehouse belonging to Russian online retailer Ozon, according to Reuters.

Russian strikes killed 6 people in Ukraine the day after the Kryvyi Rih shopping complex attack, while a Ukrainian drone struck a home in southern Russia, killing two children and injuring their parents. French President Macron agreed to accelerate air defense deliveries to Ukraine following discussions with President Zelenskyy. Putin warned that Ukraine had opened a 'Pandora's box' by striking Russian economic targets, suggesting the attacks could lead to broader escalation, according to Reuters.

Ukraine's sacked former defence minister stated that President Zelenskyy has 'questions to answer' about corruption within his government and called for elections to be held in Ukraine. Zelenskyy claimed that Putin plans to draft 300,000 new troops following Russia's September elections, according to Reuters. Norway announced it will provide over $9 billion in aid to Ukraine in 2027, according to Reuters.

Zelenskyy publicly rejected a proposal by Minister Mykhailo Fedorov to hold wartime elections, warning the idea would 'destroy' and 'split' Ukraine, calling it a 'tsunami.' Zelenskyy also stated that Trump accused him of being misleading regarding Elon Musk and Starlink, on which Ukrainian forces rely heavily for battlefield communications and drone operations.

The EU approved an additional €6.1 billion in funding for Ukraine's defence. UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham traveled to Kyiv on his first foreign trip since taking office, co-chairing a meeting with European leaders on Ukraine's Independence Day, with plans to support long-range missile production; the visit came after Moscow warned of consequences over Ukraine's reported use of British drones. Ukrainian officials reported that a Russian drone guided entirely by AI and powered by an Nvidia chip killed three Ukrainians, marking a significant development in autonomous weaponry; officials noted some Russian AI drones use Nvidia microcomputers sourced through resale markets that are virtually impossible to track, with Nvidia stating it does not sell directly to Russia. Former U.S. Vice President Mike Pence argued that giving Ukraine the capability to intercept Russian ballistic missiles would remove what he called Putin's 'last fighting tool.'

Ukraine is set to receive blueprints for the SCALP/Storm Shadow cruise missile, according to Newsweek, and the UK and Ukraine signed an artificial intelligence defence partnership focused on battlefield technology. Russia's Perm oil refinery halted operations following a drone attack on August 21, according to Reuters sources. Bradley Townsend, a Briton from South Yorkshire, was killed while fighting for Russia in Ukraine; he had left home in April telling family he was traveling to Romania.

Ukraine marked its 35th Independence Day under renewed Russian bombardment. The UK confirmed it will share classified technical information with Ukraine to support domestic production of long-range SCALP missiles, with defense firm MBDA set to release details on UK-made components.

A drone attack struck Russia's Afipsky oil refinery and a gas plant in the Krasnodar region, killing two people and sparking a fire, in an attack Ukraine carried out targeting Russian energy infrastructure. The Vatican's Foreign Minister visited Moscow and stated the war in Ukraine must end. Ousted Ukrainian Defence Minister stated in an exclusive Reuters interview that Ukraine needs changes to avoid losing the war. UK Prime Minister Burnham agreed during his Kyiv visit to raise Ukraine's appeal for Patriot interceptor missiles with the United States at the upcoming UN General Assembly.

Ukrainian drone attacks on Moscow resumed overnight into Wednesday, according to city Mayor Sergey Sobyanin, hours after a visit to the region by CIA Director William Burns. Ukraine conducted a drone strike targeting Wildberries, Russia's largest online retailer, in at least a second such attack on the company. Fuel companies in Ukraine urged customers not to linger at petrol stations following a wave of deadly Russian attacks on fuel infrastructure, as Ukraine simultaneously conducted strikes on Russian oil refineries.

Ukrainian President Zelensky awarded SpaceX CEO Elon Musk the Order of Freedom, one of Ukraine's highest state honors, for providing Starlink satellite internet access during the war. Reuters reported that prominent Ukrainian commanders have been assigned to lead the defense of the eastern region Russia has demanded, with no further details provided.

EU member states have revived a plan to use frozen Russian assets to support Ukraine, according to a Financial Times report cited by Reuters. Russian troops are attempting to infiltrate the overgrown reservoir basin of a dam destroyed three years ago, while Ukrainian soldiers engage them in close-quarters combat in the area, according to the NY Times.

Russia's Foreign Ministry warned it could target the United Kingdom after Ukraine fired British long-range cruise missiles at targets inside Russia, calling the strikes 'terrorism.' CIA Director Ratcliffe made a surprise visit to Moscow and delivered a bleak assessment of Russia's war, with CIA analysts raising concerns that Putin's advisers may not be providing him with honest assessments of the conflict, according to the NY Times. President Trump described the Moscow trip as 'semi-routine.'

Russian forces struck Kyiv and surrounding cities for a fifth consecutive day, with repeated attacks on warehouses leaving some supermarket shelves bare across the capital. Ukraine reported that Russian strikes have destroyed approximately 12 million books by hitting publishers and churches, with the destruction occurring ahead of Ukraine's first week back at school. Russian forces continued advancing, leaving another Ukrainian town in ruins as they pushed closer to additional settlements.

Russian strikes on Kyiv have continued, with jet-powered drone attacks causing disruptions including empty supermarket shelves and widespread anxiety among residents. Putin is reportedly considering escalating the war as he faces domestic difficulties, according to Newsmax, though no specific escalation plans were detailed.

Russia struck the Kyiv region for a sixth consecutive day, killing nine people and injuring over a dozen, with a separate strike on rail workers in the capital injuring 17, including two children. Russia then launched a massive coordinated aerial assault using over 200 drones alongside anti-radar, ballistic, and cruise missiles, killing 12 people and injuring more than a dozen across Ukraine.

Indian Prime Minister Modi publicly urged President Putin to end the war in Ukraine, with BBC correspondents analyzing the appeal's potential impact on Russia. A Putin envoy separately warned that the Russian economy risks going 'berserk' as it continues its shift to a war footing.
Culiacán in northern Sinaloa state is experiencing a significant surge in cartel-linked violence.
El Mencho, a top figure in Mexico's criminal underworld and associated with the Sinaloa Cartel, died.

Trump held the inaugural Shield of the Americas summit in Doral, Florida and announced a new military coalition aimed at eradicating drug cartels in the Western Hemisphere. Kristi Noem was appointed as Special Envoy for the Shield of the Americas after being removed as DHS Secretary.
The US Coast Guard intercepted a semi-submersible vessel in the Pacific Ocean carrying 17,600 pounds of cocaine.
The US military struck an alleged drug trafficking vessel in the Pacific, killing two people and leaving three survivors.
The DEA named a Colombian leader a priority target and prosecutors are probing ties between the Colombian leader and drug traffickers.
An undocumented MS-13 gang member from El Salvador was sentenced to 35 years in prison in Southern California for a murder connected to a 2019 gang arrest.
The Colombian navy shut down 30 drug labs, seized 2 tons of cocaine, and seized thousands of gallons of smuggled fuel.

Érick Valencia Salazar, a co-founder of the Jalisco New Generation drug cartel, was extradited to the United States from Mexico as part of a group of 29 alleged drug lords and subsequently pleaded guilty.

Ten current and former Mexican officials, including Sinaloa state Governor Rubén Rocha Moya, have been charged in a U.S. federal indictment for drug trafficking offenses connected to the Sinaloa Cartel.
Sinaloa Governor Rubén Rocha Moya has stepped down from his position following the U.S. federal drug trafficking charges filed against him.

U.S. drug czar Sara Carter issued a warning about medetomidine, a veterinary sedative known as a 'rhino tranquilizer,' appearing in the U.S. drug supply mixed with fentanyl and linked to American deaths, amid the administration's escalating cartel crackdown.

Mexican military captured Isai 'N,' nephew of former Sinaloa cartel leader Joaquín 'El Chapo' Guzmán, during a security operation in Nogales, Sonora, near the U.S.-Mexico border. Mexican official Omar Hamid Garcia Harfuch confirmed the arrest and noted the suspect has an extradition order.
Reuters reported on a paper trail linking a U.S. fuel trader to a notorious Mexican cartel, though specific individuals and the cartel involved were not identified in available reporting.
Ismael 'El Mayo' Zambada, co-founder of the Sinaloa cartel, was sentenced to life in prison by a federal court in Brooklyn, New York, and ordered to forfeit $15 billion.

National Review published an analysis questioning whether a leniency arrangement in Ismael 'El Mayo' Zambada's case could indicate he is cooperating with U.S. authorities and providing information on corruption within Mexico's political class.

U.S. forces targeted Juan Carlos Gonzalez, known as 'Pelon,' a California-born leader of the Jalisco New Generation Cartel (CJNG) and stepson of cartel founder 'El Mencho,' who was reportedly injured in a military operation and later died.
Mexican drug cartels have begun outsourcing methamphetamine production to Nigeria, with West Africa emerging as a growing hub for illicit drug manufacturing and export, according to BBC News.

Seven charred bodies were found in a house in Ecuador accompanied by narco gang-related messages, according to CBS News, amid the country's ongoing crisis as a cocaine trafficking hub with gang ties to Mexican and Colombian cartels.

Antonio Oseguera Cervantes, brother of CJNG leader 'El Mencho,' pleaded guilty to U.S. drug charges, with federal prosecutors stating he worked in the cartel alongside his brother Nemesio Rubén Oseguera Cervantes.

Mexican authorities arrested Ramón Ángel Álvarez Ayala, the alleged leader of the Los Rs cartel faction linked to CJNG, in connection with the livestreamed murder of influencer Valeria Márquez and the assassination of a mayor.
The U.S. announced rewards totaling more than $100 million for information leading to eight CJNG leaders, as part of the Trump administration's efforts to dismantle the cartel's top ranks.
The U.S. government suspended all official operations in Mexico's western Michoacán State, citing a threat against American interests, according to Fox News.

The FBI apprehended Gregory Henderson Jr., a fugitive with alleged Sinaloa Cartel ties, just three days after he was added to the FBI Ten Most Wanted list, with FBI Director Kash Patel announcing the capture.

Nevada man Luis Alberto Osorio admitted to purchasing 140 firearms, including military-style rifles, and funneling them to violent Mexican drug-trafficking organizations in a straw purchase scheme, according to the DOJ.
Osorio faces up to 70 years in prison, with sentencing scheduled for February, according to the DOJ.

Sinaloa Governor Rubén Rocha Moya, who has been accused by the U.S. of aiding a cartel, left office again after briefly returning, following widespread criticism from members of his own party and others.

The DOJ announced federal grand jury indictments against two Jalisco New Generation Cartel regional commanders, brothers Ramon Alvarez Ayala (44) and Rafael Alvarez Ayala (42), on charges of trafficking cocaine and methamphetamine into the United States and committing firearms offenses.
A two-year war between rival Sinaloa Cartel factions in Mexico has driven a surge in killings and disappearances targeting women, according to the NY Times.
Iranian authorities are conducting mass arrests of protesters and reformists following a deadly crackdown on anti-government protests.
The Iranian national women's football team returned to Iran after several players withdrew asylum requests.
Iran executed three individuals arrested in connection with protests, as announced by Iran's judiciary.
Iran executed three men, including Saleh Mohammadi, a young member of Iran's national wrestling team; these were the first executions carried out over January protests in Iran.
A State Department spokesperson called Iran's executions 'barbaric'; the UN and activist groups report Iran's regime is using the death penalty to crush dissent.
Iran's judiciary reported that two men involved in January protests were executed.
Iran has carried out executions by hanging, including of teenagers.
Iran released a Japanese national on bail who had been jailed amid antigovernment protests. The released individual is believed to be Shinnosuke Kawashima, NHK's Tehran bureau chief.

CENTCOM announced a new wave of strikes against Iranian command centers and air defense sites, concluding at 9 p.m. EST. Trump stated he is open to ordering the military to eliminate Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps, drawing a comparison to the campaign against ISIS.

Satellite imagery revealed that Iran's Bushehr nuclear power plant sustained strike damage between July 7 and 12. Oil prices spiked more than 4% and U.S. gas prices approached $4 per gallon as traffic through the Strait of Hormuz declined.
