Two U.S. service members were killed and one is missing following an Iranian ballistic missile and drone attack on a U.S. base in Jordan on July 17; CENTCOM confirmed the casualties on Saturday. Iranian Supreme Leader Khamenei stated that U.S. breaches of agreements demonstrate that President Trump's signature is 'worthless.' U.S. overnight strikes damaged a tunnel and three bridges in Iran's Hormozgan Province, leaving residents isolated, while critical water and power infrastructure damage is being compounded by temperatures exceeding 100 degrees across the region.

Iran launched missile and drone attacks on U.S. Gulf allies Kuwait and Bahrain, causing a fire at a Kuwait power plant, with air raid sirens also reported in Jordan. Retired Admiral James Stavridis warned the U.S. to monitor the Suez Canal, saying Iran is making noise about attempting to close it using Houthi forces. Energy Secretary Chris Wright stated the mission in Iran will continue, while Jordan emerged as a more prominent U.S. basing partner as other regional allies restricted Washington's use of their airspace and facilities.

Analysts warned that escalating strikes risk spiraling into a wider conflict neither side can contain, urging a swift return to negotiations.

Houthi forces declared a blockade of Red Sea oil routes amid the ongoing U.S.-Iran exchange of strikes, while analysts assessed that Iran is targeting Gulf states to pressure Washington while avoiding direct confrontation with U.S. naval assets.

The U.S. launched its 10th consecutive night of strikes on Iran, with explosions reported in Bandar Abbas, Qeshm Island, Chabahar, and Konarak. Nearly 100 U.S. service members have sustained injuries since the campaign began, while GOP lawmakers are pressing Trump to reopen the Strait of Hormuz as quickly as possible, citing rising oil prices and potential voter backlash. Keith Kellogg called for the deployment of U.S. ground troops in Iran and replacement of the current American negotiating team. Al Jazeera separately reported that some of the worst fighting in months has erupted thirty days after the signing of a U.S.-Iran Memorandum of Understanding, threatening to unravel the ceasefire agreement.

The Pentagon identified Sgt. Michael Emmanuel Swinton, 30, of Fayetteville, N.C., as the U.S. service member killed at Erbil Air Base, Iraq, during a controlled detonation of unexploded ordnance from a downed Iranian drone, raising the confirmed U.S. death toll to 17. Defense Secretary Hegseth and Gen. Dan Caine testified before the Senate Appropriations Committee on Tuesday regarding an $87.6 billion supplemental funding request for the Iran war. Trump, during an Oval Office meeting with Lebanese President Aoun, stated the U.S. could strike Pickaxe Mountain in Iran 'very soon and very heavily,' while several Fox News pundits urged de-escalation, warning the conflict could become a political liability with midterm elections approximately 100 days away.

Tehran claimed it retaliated for U.S. strikes by targeting American assets in Kuwait, Bahrain, and Jordan. A CIA assessment concluded Iran would not capitulate or abandon its nuclear program in response to U.S. military strikes. Rep. Rich McCormick (R-Ga.) criticized the administration's prior memorandum of understanding with Iran, saying the U.S. should have 'finished the job' earlier, while Sen. Bill Hagerty (R-TN) compared the current situation to Truman's firing of Gen. MacArthur during the Korean War.

The U.S. military conducted its 11th consecutive night of strikes on Iran, with new explosions reported; oil prices rose slightly following the announcement. Defense Secretary Hegseth confirmed the Iran war has cost the U.S. $37.5 billion so far, while the broader defense budget request under discussion totals $1.5 trillion, with approximately $70 billion allocated for Iran war operations. During Senate Appropriations Committee testimony, Sen. Gary Peters called Hegseth a 'failure' and characterized the war as 'an utter and complete failure,' while Democrats broadly expressed skepticism about additional funding. House Speaker Mike Johnson urged Trump to 'wrap it up' in Iran, while Trump rejected that midterm considerations would influence his strategy. The U.S. military identified Sgt. Angel S. Rampersad as the third American service member believed killed in the Iranian drone attack on a U.S. base in Jordan, and Iran claimed a new attack on a U.S. base in Kuwait.

President Trump attended a dignified transfer ceremony at Dover Air Force Base on Wednesday for four U.S. service members killed in the war with Iran — 1st Lt. Tyler J. Feehan, Sgt. Michael E. Swinton, Sgt. Angel S. Rampersad, and Pvt. Isabella Gonzales — with Defense Secretary Hegseth also in attendance. The deaths occurred in Jordan and Iraq after the temporary ceasefire with Iran collapsed. Trump warned Iran would 'pay the price' for the deaths, and separately threatened to strike one Iranian bridge or power plant for every Iranian attack on ships in the Strait of Hormuz, framing the threat as a new red line and an escalation of strategy. Oil prices surged nearly 5%, rising past $95 per barrel, as prospects for new peace talks dimmed following the 11th consecutive night of strikes; the national average gas price rose to just over $4 per gallon, up 91 cents from a year ago according to AAA. Secretary of State Rubio warned that Iran's military control of the Strait of Hormuz sets a 'dangerous precedent' and said Iran is in 'a lot of trouble.' CBS News sources indicated the true cost of the war is likely higher than the $37.5 billion figure Hegseth provided to Congress, while the Pentagon has requested an additional $67–70 billion to replenish depleted weapons stockpiles.

Iran's chief nuclear negotiator warned that if Iran's security is not guaranteed, 'no infrastructure will be safe.' The U.S. launched new strikes hitting multiple Iranian cities including Sirik, Ahvaz, and Bushehr, while the Pentagon briefed a bipartisan group of House lawmakers on the conflict. Bill Cassidy identified as a potential decisive vote. The NY Times published analysis of video footage and satellite imagery revealing new damage details from Iranian strikes on U.S. military sites, while Jordan is assessed as unlikely to restrict American military presence despite ongoing Iranian airstrikes.

The U.S. conducted its 12th consecutive night of strikes against Iran, with Secretary of State Rubio warning that 'every night the price gets higher' and characterizing U.S. policy as a 'head for an eye' in response to Iran's stated 'eye for an eye' stance. President Trump warned Thursday that the U.S. will hold Iran accountable for any Houthi attacks on commercial shipping following the strikes on two Saudi tankers. Reuters sources reported that Iran transferred IRGC commanders and missile equipment to Houthi forces in Yemen. Rand Paul stated the U.S. is 'worse off' than before the conflict began and called the war 'not a success.'

Trump warned of the largest strikes on Iran yet following Iranian attacks targeting Bahrain, Kuwait, and Jordan, and told Axios he is nearing a decision on launching a 'massive attack' described as 'bigger than ever before.' Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi warned that 'mindless aggression' would not help reach a deal. The total U.S. war cost is now reported at nearly $110 billion, with the Trump administration seeking an additional $67 billion; analysts noted voting against war funding remains politically difficult for members of Congress. The Pentagon's website showed a lower U.S. troop death count than publicly acknowledged, with three military officials and a Pentagon spokesman giving conflicting explanations for the discrepancy; the NY Times separately reported the death of Sgt. Michael Emmanuel Swinton brings confirmed U.S. fatalities to 18. An Iranian military group warned the UK that British bases used by U.S. forces are 'legitimate targets,' prompting the UK to declare it is 'ready to defend itself.' Trump announced that Iranian funds under U.S. control will be used to compensate damages to ships and cargo resulting from the war, and the Trump administration expressed concern that the U.S. defense industrial base cannot produce missiles fast enough to replenish interceptor and precision-guided munitions being expended. Iranians report that months of war, ongoing strikes, and economic crisis have brought daily life to a standstill, with many residents abandoning work and future plans.

Netanyahu is scheduled to travel to Washington on Monday and meet with Trump at the White House on Tuesday, coinciding with his attendance at memorial services for the late Sen. Lindsey Graham. Trump warned Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin it would be 'very bad' if either country is found supplying weapons to Iran, though he subsequently stated on Truth Social that he takes both leaders at face value that they are not doing so. Rep. Thomas Massie accused Defense Secretary Hegseth of 'breaking the law' by allegedly framing the conflict as two separate wars to avoid seeking congressional authorization. Senate Republican Policy Committee Chair Shelley Moore Capito stated the American public is 'growing weary' of the conflict, which Trump initially said would last four to five weeks but has now continued for nearly five months, while S&P surveys indicate the U.S. economy had been accelerating before failed peace talks disrupted momentum by triggering an oil price surge and renewed inflation concerns.

U.S. military commanders are intentionally allowing some Iranian missiles and drones to bypass air defenses to preserve dwindling interceptor stockpiles, according to two senior U.S. officials cited by NBC News. President Trump departed the NATO summit in Turkey aboard an older Air Force One aircraft after U.S. officials received a credible threat from Iran and allied proxy groups, with the New York Times separately reporting the last-minute aircraft swap; a Times investigation also found Trump's push to accelerate delivery of a new Air Force One led to ballooning costs and safety trade-offs. The Pentagon faced renewed criticism after its official count of U.S. troops killed in the conflict dropped from 18 to 14, deepening questions about discrepancies in the official death toll. Former Defense Secretary Leon Panetta warned the U.S. is in 'deep trouble,' comparing the conflict to Vietnam, while Sen. Tim Sheehy delivered an emotional floor speech opposing the Iran War Powers Resolution. Rising gas prices driven by the conflict and Trump tariffs are fueling renewed inflation concerns, and experts expressed skepticism that an intensified strike campaign targeting infrastructure would force Tehran to capitulate.

U.S. Special Operations Forces are reportedly positioned near Iran and prepared to launch what sources describe as the 'most sophisticated operation in military history,' potentially involving thousands of troops storming Iranian nuclear facilities to recover enriched uranium, according to the New York Post. New polling indicates the escalating war is threatening to depress Republican voter turnout in midterm battlegrounds, with Trump's MAGA base showing increasing opposition to the conflict. The U.S. Treasury Department announced sanctions against nine firms and four individuals connected to sanctioned Iranian billionaire financier Babak Zanjani for attempting to evade existing sanctions.

U.S.-Iran fighting paused for a second consecutive day, with Trump delaying escalation plans partly due to dwindling interceptor missile stockpiles, according to American officials cited by the NY Times, which also described Trump as 'frustrated and erratic' and constrained in his options despite commanding significant military power. The U.S. military released footage showing forces boarding and disabling a tanker accused of breaking the Iran blockade. UK Defence Secretary Wes Streeting warned Britain stands ready to respond to any Iranian attacks, dismissing Iranian actions as 'sabre-rattling.' Houthi rebels launched missiles and drone attacks on Saudi Arabia in apparent retaliation for Saudi strikes on a Yemeni coastal city, opening a new front in the conflict.

UN Ambassador Mike Waltz appeared on NBC's Meet the Press, asserting the U.S. military has 'everything that it needs' for operations against Iran and attributing depleted munitions stockpiles to the Biden administration. The NY Times reported Trump held off on authorizing a major escalation partly due to adviser concerns over dangerously diminished air defense stockpiles. Both the U.S. and Iran confirmed a pause in direct strikes for a second consecutive day on Sunday, with negotiations on an interim ceasefire continuing, according to NPR. Sen. Bill Cassidy called for a national discussion and urged Trump to go to Congress to find a path to peace, saying an early end to the war 'seems unlikely,' while Sen. John Kennedy stated on CBS he supports continuing the blockade. A CBS News poll found most Americans believe the conflict has proven harder than Trump anticipated, with respondents expecting it to last months or years longer. Anti-war protesters gathered outside a UK airbase demanding an end to U.S. use of the facility for strikes on Iran, while the conflict broadened as Iran accused Ukraine of targeting one of its vessels in the Caspian Sea.

Oil prices fell sharply and U.S. stock-index futures rallied on Monday as the two-day pause in U.S.-Iran strikes raised hopes of a diplomatic resolution. Oman-mediated talks on reopening the Strait of Hormuz made progress, with the U.S. halting strikes for a second consecutive night as a result, per CBS News sources. The Pentagon further revised its casualty reporting, separating figures across two web pages in a move the NY Times noted could make it harder to tally the full toll, while ABC News reported 18 service members killed and more than 600 wounded since the war began — figures at odds with earlier official counts. Iranian Supreme Leader Khamenei conditioned any potential U.S.-Iran peace deal on an end to Israeli military operations in Lebanon. Republican senators warned that confidence in Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is eroding, and Sen. John Kennedy stated Trump favors resuming daily strikes rather than pausing for negotiations. Asian nations accelerated efforts to reduce reliance on imported fuels amid supply disruptions caused by the war, and CENTCOM's chief reportedly urged a halt to strikes, according to Newsmax.
The U.S.-Iran conflict entered its sixth month, with both sides assessing their next moves amid continued uncertainty over the diplomatic pause, according to the NY Times.

A Reuters/Ipsos poll released Tuesday found only 33% of Americans approve of U.S. military strikes on Iran, with 62% disapproving. Iran's IRGC-affiliated Tasnim News Agency released a propaganda video titled 'Where to Kill Melania?!' targeting First Lady Melania Trump and her son Barron, prompting the U.S. Secret Service to launch a probe into the Iran-linked assassination threat. Trump threatened to 'take out' Pickaxe Mountain in Iran if a nuclear deal is not reached, while separately describing ongoing talks as 'good.' Houthi attacks have now threatened Saudi Arabia's alternative oil export route through its interior pipeline network, which the kingdom had been relying on to bypass Strait of Hormuz disruptions. Trump administration officials stated Iran is increasingly desperate for cash as U.S. sanctions continue to take effect, while Americans' economic confidence declined in the month following escalating U.S.-Iran tensions as gas prices rose again.

Iran launched multiple ballistic missiles at U.S. forces in the Middle East on Tuesday evening, which the U.S. military intercepted. Iran launched a surprise ballistic missile attack targeting U.S. forces in Jordan on Wednesday, prompting Trump to vow in a Fox News interview to 'beat the f—ing s—' out of Iran in response. Global oil prices surged 7%, crossing above $90 a barrel, following the attack and Trump's retaliation vow, with West Texas Intermediate and Brent crude front-month contracts both climbing sharply. Alex Jones called for Trump's impeachment over the Iran war and warned on his live show that a national draft is being prepared in connection with the conflict.

The U.S. military launched a heavy wave of airstrikes against dozens of IRGC targets in Iran, characterizing the strikes as 'a powerful response' to Iran's ballistic missile attack on a U.S. base in Jordan. Drone strikes hit Egypt's Mediterranean port of Damietta on Wednesday, sparking fires on two natural gas vessels, according to CBS News, marking a geographic expansion of conflict linked to the war. University of Chicago professor Robert Pape described the Strait of Hormuz and Iran's nuclear capabilities as 'zero-sum' issues blocking progress, while Vice President Vance stated he is 'extremely hopeful' Tehran will disavow nuclear weapons.

Iran released Dena Karari, a dual Iranian-American citizen who had been held on espionage charges since December 2024 when her passport was seized. President Trump announced the release Wednesday evening, describing it as a 'gesture of goodwill' from Iran.

A disputed paragraph concerning the Strait of Hormuz is placing strain on a U.S.-Iran deal, according to the Washington Post. The release of a U.S. citizen by Iran, previously reported as announced by Trump, was separately confirmed by the Washington Post as a goodwill gesture.
The New York Times profiled four key negotiators involved in potential U.S.-Iran diplomatic talks, noting that agreeing on a shared goal would be the critical first step in any future negotiations.
Iran announced it is suspending its commitments to an interim deal with the United States.

Trump called on Congress to add Iran to a bipartisan Russia sanctions bill, invoking the memory of its late author, former Sen. Lindsey Graham of South Carolina, in support of the measure. CBS News separately confirmed that the dual Iranian-American citizen previously reported as released has departed Iran and returned home.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated the U.S. remains open to diplomacy with Iran following the ninth consecutive night of U.S. bombing campaigns, adding that Iran has signaled it wants to negotiate even as both sides continue to escalate attacks.

Mediators have proposed a 10-day ceasefire to revive an interim deal between Iran and the United States, according to a senior Iranian official speaking to Reuters. A coalition of terrorism victims is demanding Iran pay restitution to victims of Iranian-sponsored terror before any funds are unfrozen as part of a potential peace deal.

A delegation of survivors of Iranian-sponsored terrorism and their families traveled to Washington, D.C., to demand that President Trump include restitution from Tehran as a condition of any peace deal with Iran.

Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaid traveled to Tehran following a high-profile meeting with President Trump, according to Al Jazeera. Analysts describe the U.S. as having returned to a pressure campaign against Iran following the collapse of the temporary ceasefire period.
China has initiated a push for Pakistan and Iran to explore pathways toward new talks with the United States, according to Reuters sources.
President Trump stated on Friday that while the U.S. is engaged in ongoing talks with Iran following nearly two weeks of strikes, he does not believe Tehran is ready to make a deal yet.

Iran's government publicly accused state broadcaster IRIB of censorship after portions of President Pezeshkian's speech were not aired, with IRIB rejecting what it called 'improper attributions,' as mediators continued pushing for Iran-U.S. talks.

U.S. Ambassador to the UN Waltz stated Trump is giving Iran nuclear talks 'a little bit of room,' signaling a continued diplomatic window, according to Reuters. An Iranian source told Reuters that Iran will halt attacks as long as the U.S. maintains its pause, following reports that Trump called off planned strikes.

A new diplomatic push launched Sunday following the weekend pause in fighting, with NBC News reporting active efforts to potentially end the war. The U.S. Ambassador confirmed Trump paused strikes specifically to create space for diplomatic talks, with neither side launching attacks over two consecutive nights. The two-day halt was directly linked to progress in Oman-mediated negotiations, according to CBS News sources, amid growing U.S. concerns over depleted munitions stockpiles.

The U.S. and Iran began formally exchanging diplomatic messages following nearly two weeks of intense fighting, while Iranian Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei publicly stated Iran is not currently seeking negotiations with the United States. A CBS News poll found more than two-thirds of Americans think the Trump administration should end the war, with a majority disapproving of the conflict and over half expressing uncertainty and frustration. Oil prices fell nearly 10 percent on Monday, with Brent Crude dropping below $91 per barrel and WTI falling to approximately $84 per barrel, after prices had surpassed $100 per barrel on Friday. Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu stated Iran is the top agenda item in his meeting with Trump, while Trump told reporters aboard Air Force One he would ask Vladimir Putin whether Russia is sharing satellite imagery of U.S. bases in the Middle East with Iran. Rep. Tom Barrett (R-MI) broke with Trump on Iran policy, marking a notable departure from the Republican mainstream.

For a third consecutive day, the U.S. and Iran held fire as Qatari and Pakistani mediators worked to restart ceasefire talks. Trump publicly confirmed talks with Iran are taking place during the strike pause, while Iran denied that direct talks are occurring, with CBS News reporting indirect conversations are ongoing. Trump threatened to resume military strikes if diplomatic talks fail. Iranian leaders showed no urgency to resume ceasefire talks, with analysts noting Iran is betting it can outlast U.S. pressure and leverage its control over the Strait of Hormuz. Netanyahu arrived in Washington for talks with Trump, as Iran described the U.S. as 'struggling' to end the five-month-old war. Oil prices fell a further approximately 1% as investors assessed the ongoing strike pause.

Trump stated there is a 'good chance' of progress in talks with Iran, with negotiators working to resolve a deadlock over transit fees and management of the Strait of Hormuz, according to Al Jazeera. Oil prices fell further as Brent crude and WTI contracts declined after Trump claimed 'deep talks' are underway, per the Wall Street Journal. Al Jazeera reports analysts assess Iran's economy has continued to withstand prolonged U.S. sanctions pressure, with the population expected to absorb further economic shockwaves.

Hundreds of Jordanian political, legal, and other public figures signed an open letter warning that Jordan's close alliance with the United States poses a risk to the kingdom, demanding the withdrawal of American troops.
Former U.S. Ambassador to the UAE Barbara Leaf warned via Al Jazeera that U.S. escalation with Iran is 'fairly pointless' as military exchanges between the two sides continued to intensify.

Retired Vice Admiral Robert Harward, former Deputy Commander of Central Command, stated Thursday that the calculus for the Iranian government is changing, citing external and internal pressures as well as ongoing cyberattacks against Iran.

Trump called off a planned 'massive' military attack on Iran that had been scheduled for the weekend, stating he is 'not looking to kill people' and that an agreement is imminent. A new round of U.S.-Iran negotiations is scheduled for Monday, brokered by Saudi Arabia, the UAE, and Qatar. Trump also called for the immediate reopening of the Strait of Hormuz as part of any prospective deal. Oil prices tumbled and gold prices rose following the cancellation of the planned strikes, while the Japanese yen spiked sharply amid apparent currency market intervention. Iran, however, stated there are no current talks taking place with the United States. Experts cited by the NY Times said Iran's expansion of regional fighting sent a warning about the dangers of a widening war, with Trump's reversal interpreted as a signal of Tehran's leverage in the conflict.

Trump called Iran 'duplicitous' and warned that current negotiations represent a 'last chance' for a peace deal, threatening 'decapitation' if Iran fails to reach an agreement. Iran clarified that its talks are being conducted with Oman, not directly with the United States. Former National Counterterrorism Center Director Joe Kent argued Trump should declare victory against Iran and withdraw U.S. troops from the Middle East. Trump claimed that 'Iran's march toward nuclear weapons has been halted and reversed,' according to Newsweek, amid questions about shifting public support for his administration's Iran policy.

Trump again warned Iran of a 'last chance' to make a peace deal, threatening 'decapitation' if negotiations fail, according to The Hill. Iran clarified it is conducting talks through Oman rather than directly with the United States, and denied any resumption of talks despite Trump announcing diplomacy would resume Monday. According to the NY Times, an emerging deal brokered through Oman would reopen the Strait of Hormuz but would grant Iran new strategic leverage it did not possess before the conflict began.

Pakistan has launched a new diplomatic push to sustain US-Iran talks amid deepening mistrust, as repeated ceasefire failures have exposed the limits of ongoing mediation efforts, according to Al Jazeera.
President Trump stated that the United States and Iran are having 'very good discussions,' according to Reuters.

The US removed sanctions from three entities linked to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, according to updates on the Treasury Department's website. Former U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations Mark Wallace said Iran is 'uncertain' on how to handle President Trump as both countries enter talks on a potential interim peace deal, according to The Hill.

Iranian parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf accused Trump of conducting 'show diplomacy on loop,' dismissing Trump's claims of ongoing talks and his assertion that any war would end 'pretty soon.'
The Trump administration announced its eighth round of Iran-related sanctions this year, targeting Iran's banking system and companies, according to CBS News.

Iranian National Security Council Secretary Mohammad Bagher Zolghadr released a list of six demands through state media that the U.S. must fulfill before any Strait of Hormuz peace deal, complicating ongoing negotiations. Vice President JD Vance acknowledged progress in talks with Iran but warned the situation remains unresolved, describing it as still 'in the middle of the game.'

Iranian President Pezeshkian expressed hope that Oman-mediated talks could resolve the 'neither war nor peace' state of US-Iran relations. Iranian Foreign Minister stated that direct talks with the United States will not proceed while the interim nuclear deal remains in breach, according to Reuters. A senior Iranian security official simultaneously issued broader conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, underscoring internal divisions between diplomatic and hardline positions.

Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi stated there are no ongoing negotiations between Tehran and Washington, while Al Jazeera analysts described the two sides as 'talking past each other' without meaningful progress toward an agreement.
Former Defense Secretary Mark Esper stated that Iran's new demands during Hormuz negotiations indicate Tehran believes it is negotiating from a position of strength.

The Trump administration shifted its approach toward Iran, opting to increase economic pressure rather than pursue military action, according to Al Jazeera. Trump publicly characterized the situation as 'like a chess game' and said the U.S. is 'low-keying it,' describing negotiations as only 'semi' ongoing while noting Iran is suffering from 'huge inflation' and lack of funds. Trump separately dismissed Iran's demand for war reparations, according to AP News. Additional U.S. sanctions against Iran were announced amid continued uncertainty over the Strait of Hormuz talks.
Pakistan's government stated that the U.S. and Iran are close to reaching 'some sort' of deal, despite ongoing attacks on shipping in the region.
Mediators are working to restart US-Iran dialogue amid a continued standoff in the Strait of Hormuz, but negotiations remain at a standstill, according to Al Jazeera.

White House deputy national security advisor Andy Baker, who played a central role in Iran peace negotiations, is set to leave the Trump administration in the coming weeks, marking the second high-profile White House departure of the week, according to Axios.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated that no decision has been made on returning to talks with the U.S., while indicating Iran is working through Oman as a diplomatic channel and that Strait of Hormuz shipping access is conditional on the U.S. meeting certain conditions.

Iran called on the U.S. to 'accept the reality of defeat and stop indulging in delusions' in response to Trump's suggestion that he would declare the Strait of Hormuz U.S. territory. State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott addressed the situation with Iran and the revocation of U.S. visas affecting hundreds of thousands of foreign nationals in an NPR interview.

Trump confirmed the existence of a direct backchannel with Iran's IRGC for peace talks while simultaneously issuing a bombing warning to Oman and calling for Iran's 'white flag of surrender' as the ceasefire deadline expired. Iran warned it will escalate if the U.S. does not honor an unspecified deal within weeks, according to Reuters.
Turkish President Erdogan urged Trump to pursue diplomatic talks with Iran and offered Turkey's support in facilitating the process, according to Reuters.

The expiration of the 60-day ceasefire deadline without a deal rattled financial markets, with the yield on the 30-year U.S. Treasury bond rising to its highest level in nearly 20 years and U.S. stocks falling, according to the NY Times and Reuters. The U.S. and Iran are reported to be far apart on terms, with NPR noting the stalemate has continued to deplete U.S. resources.

Trump posted on social media that there are no ongoing or planned talks with Iran, amid reports of mixed messaging from the White House on U.S.-Iran communications. South Korea's foreign minister stated that Trump appears to be using pressure over Iran-related issues as leverage over Seoul regarding investment, according to Reuters.

Iran warned Gulf countries against assisting the U.S. military, while Iran's foreign minister stated Tehran will not accept a ceasefire but only a comprehensive agreement to fully end the war, even as Trump suggested peace talks might resume 'maybe at some point.'

Trump threatened Iran with 'economic warfare and isolation on an unprecedented scale,' which Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi dismissed as a 'diversion from America's own crisis,' warning it would result in 'further defeat' for the United States. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent stated that economic pressure could potentially avert major military operations and urged allies to support plans to 'squash' Iran's economy, warning partners they must decide whether they 'are with us or against us.' Newsweek reported that as U.S. national debt approaches $40 trillion with consumer prices elevated, the pressure campaign carries domestic political and fiscal risks for Republicans, while U.S. farmers face rising war-linked costs that could influence tight midterm races.

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian stated it is time to end the war with the U.S. from 'a position of strength,' as Omani and Iranian foreign ministers held a call amid Washington's preparations for new sanctions.

Iran escalated its warnings to neighboring countries, stating that any state joining the US economic campaign against Tehran would be considered an enemy and face 'tit-for-tat' retaliation, describing the US effort as an 'economic D-Day.' Iran also announced that Pakistan's army chief is scheduled to visit Tehran, according to Reuters.

Iran's Supreme National Security Council leader Mohsen Rezaei escalated warnings to Middle Eastern neighbors, vowing to prevent 'a single drop of oil' from leaving the region if Iran is targeted by US-led economic pressure. Iran separately dismissed the threatened new US sanctions as the actions of a 'desperate' party, asserting the measures would fail.
The US announced and formally implemented a new expanded sanctions package against Iran, with Iran vowing retaliation in response to the widened measures.

The U.S. sanctioned Chinese firms over their links to Iran while sparing major banks, as Washington and Beijing prepared for key diplomatic talks. China's Foreign Ministry condemned the approach, stating the sanctions would 'further intensify tensions and conflicts, create spillover risks.' The Iranian rial fell to an all-time low under the pressure campaign, prompting expert debate over whether maximum economic pressure could destabilize the Iranian regime. The U.S. separately announced a $10 million reward for intelligence on Iranian leaders.

The US expanded its economic pressure campaign by threatening sanctions against any country or entity engaging with Iran's gold, digital assets, aviation, shipping, and technology industries. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent called for the closure of all foreign branches of Bank Melli, Iran's largest lender. Iran is reportedly calculating that global economic pressures and Republican concerns ahead of midterm elections will force the Trump administration to back down, framing the standoff as a game of 'chicken,' according to Al Jazeera. CIA Director made a rare, unannounced visit to Moscow, marking an unusual direct engagement between US intelligence leadership and Russia.

CIA Director John Ratcliffe traveled to Moscow in a rare, unannounced visit and met with Russian intelligence counterparts, a trip confirmed by the Kremlin. Ratcliffe did not meet with President Putin, and the purpose of the visit has not been publicly disclosed.

Qatar's Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed is set to visit Tehran to pursue mediation efforts aimed at reviving stalled US-Iran diplomatic talks, according to Reuters. CIA Director Ratcliffe's Moscow visit included a warning to Russia not to attack NATO member states, according to sources familiar with the matter.

President Trump spoke with Al Jazeera and the White House stated there will be no negotiations with Iran, with officials saying all options remain on the table. Qatar's Prime Minister met with Iran's Foreign Minister in Tehran as part of ongoing mediation efforts. A temporary agreement was separately reached regarding passage through the Strait of Hormuz.
Iran has acknowledged feeling the pain of new U.S. sanctions pressure but has not changed its position or policies in response to the measures, according to the Washington Post.

Iran urged the United States to honor its commitments under the existing Memorandum of Understanding following renewed strikes in the Strait of Hormuz. The Shanghai Cooperation Organisation, at its Bishkek summit, issued a statement condemning attacks and sanctions on Iran, with SCO member state leaders convening in the aftermath of the ongoing U.S.-Iran conflict.
A U.S. military strike in the eastern Pacific Ocean on Sunday killed three people aboard a boat accused of drug trafficking.
A separate U.S. military strike targeting a boat accused of carrying drugs in the Caribbean Sea on Monday killed two people. This follows a similar strike in the eastern Pacific the previous day.

A U.S. military strike on an alleged drug-trafficking boat in the eastern Pacific Ocean killed two men, leaving one survivor. The strike is the latest in a series of such operations conducted by the military in the region.

At least 193 people have been killed in the Trump administration's campaign of missile strikes on boats claimed to be trafficking drugs in Latin American waters. A recent U.S. strike on a boat in the Eastern Pacific killed one person while two others survived, according to SOUTHCOM.
A suspect was charged with attempting to assassinate the president following a shooting at the White House Correspondents' Dinner; the charges were formally announced after the attack.

The suspect charged in the assassination attempt has been identified as Cole Allen, who has agreed to remain jailed ahead of his trial. Critics of President Trump publicly blamed his rhetoric in connection with the attack.
Cole Allen, 31, pleaded not guilty on Monday in federal court to charges related to the alleged assassination attempt against President Trump at the White House Correspondents' Association dinner.
Allen faces four total counts in the case. Monday's court proceeding was formally an arraignment, at which Allen entered not guilty pleas to all charges.

A separate incident from the Correspondents' Dinner case: U.S. Secret Service officers shot and killed a man identified as Nasire Best, 21, of Dundalk, Maryland, who opened fire at a White House security checkpoint on Saturday. CBS News reported Best had previously blocked a White House entry lane in June 2025 and had attempted to gain access to the White House the year before. A bystander was left in serious condition during the exchange of gunfire. Secret Service Director Sean Curran praised officers for their 'quick and decisive response,' and five senior law enforcement officials told NBC News that Best had a history of mental health concerns.

The rescheduled White House Correspondents' Dinner was held Friday night at the Waldorf Astoria in Washington, D.C., with enhanced security measures and a sharply reduced crowd compared to the original April event at the Washington Hilton. President Trump attended and delivered an approximately one-hour speech that included mockery of political opponents and the press, as well as jokes referencing a third term and bulletproof vests. Outgoing WHCA President Weijia Jiang of CBS News opened the event with a defiant message declaring 'We are back. We will not be intimidated.' Howard University student journalist Ssanyu Lukoma was among several student journalists honored at the dinner.

timelines.title: Taylor Swift Concert Attack Plot Investigation

entries.update: An Austrian man is on trial in Austria for allegedly plotting a terrorist attack on a Taylor Swift concert in Vienna, with prosecutors alleging ties to the Islamic State.
The Austrian trial over the foiled Taylor Swift concert attack plot has entered its final day, according to Reuters.

The 21-year-old Austrian defendant was convicted and sentenced to 15 years in prison after admitting to plotting the attack on the Taylor Swift Vienna concert along with other terrorism-related offences.
The U.S. Senate blocked a Democratic-led resolution challenging Trump's military authority over Cuba, with Republican senators voting against advancing the measure.
Cuba is experiencing severe energy disruptions due to a nationwide depletion of diesel and fuel oil stocks, with the U.S.-led embargo cited as a contributing factor to the shortage.
CIA Director John Ratcliffe met with Cuban officials in Havana on Thursday to discuss economic and security issues, with both sides confirming the meeting took place.
U.S. officials are seeking to indict former Cuban leader Raúl Castro, according to U.S. officials.

A U.S. grand jury indicted Raúl Castro, now 94, along with five others on charges including murder, conspiracy to kill U.S. nationals, and destruction of aircraft related to the 1996 shootdown of two Brothers to the Rescue civilian planes that killed four Cuban Americans. Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche announced the indictment in South Florida; Castro was Cuba's armed forces minister at the time of the incident.

The USS Nimitz carrier strike group, including the destroyer USS Gridley and an air wing of F/A-18 Super Hornets and EA-18G Growlers, arrived in the Caribbean on the same day the Justice Department announced the indictment of Raúl Castro.

CIA Director Ratcliffe brought a covert operator involved in efforts to capture Nicolás Maduro to his meeting with senior Cuban officials in Havana last week. Critics accused the Trump administration of manufacturing a pretext for a potential invasion of Cuba, citing the Castro indictment and administration statements amplifying Cuba's perceived military and intelligence threat.

Cuba issued a formal warning to the United States on Saturday, asserting its 'full and exclusive sovereignty over the airspace above its territory,' in an apparent response to the federal indictment of Raúl Castro. The U.S. Treasury Department issued subpoenas to Twitch streamer Hasan Piker and CodePink cofounder Medea Benjamin as part of a federal probe into whether the two violated U.S. sanctions by traveling to Cuba, according to Fox News.

The Trump administration released a report alleging that Cuba serves as the 'connective tissue' of a global 'anti-American coalition,' and claimed ties between the Cuban government and the American left.
Cuban President Miguel Díaz-Canel accused the United States of committing 'political genocide' against Cuba in remarks made on the anniversary of the Cuban revolution, according to Reuters.

The CIA has established a secret task force focused on Cuba, directing increased financial, human, and technical resources toward the island with the goal of creating divisions within the Cuban political elite, according to the NY Times.

A Cuba expert assessed for the Washington Examiner that the Trump administration is more likely to escalate economic and political pressure on Cuba than to pursue military intervention in the near term.
Trump, speaking at a Palm Beach forum, said the U.S. would be 'taking over' Cuba 'almost immediately,' and referenced finishing a job in Iran before turning to Cuba.

Cuba's Energy Minister Vicente de la O Levy announced on Wednesday that the country has completely exhausted its fuel oil and diesel supplies, stating 'We have absolutely no fuel (oil), and absolutely no diesel.' The minister attributed the crisis to U.S. sanctions and the blockade, which have pushed Cuba's energy system into severe collapse.

Secretary of State Rubio announced the arrest of the sister of the head of GAESA, Cuba's military business conglomerate. Rubio formally declared Cuba a national security threat to the United States, raising the prospect of military intervention, while Cuba's foreign minister accused him of spreading lies and attempting to instigate military aggression. Trump and Rubio raised the possibility of military intervention in Cuba one day after the administration announced criminal charges against former Cuban leader Raúl Castro.

Former national security adviser John Bolton warned that the Trump administration may attempt to 'kidnap or snatch' Raúl Castro, cautioning that Castro's indictment could serve as a pretext for military intervention in Cuba. The U.S. warned a peaceful agreement with Cuba is unlikely, while Havana described the situation as a 'fraudulent case' designed to justify military aggression.

Sen. Lindsey Graham declared that 'the liberation of the wonderful people of Cuba from the clutches of communism is close at hand,' backing White House threats of potential military action against the island.
The Trump administration is reportedly accelerating plans aimed at engineering the collapse of the Cuban government, according to Newsmax, though specific details of the strategy were not disclosed.
Rep. Pramila Jayapal admitted to working with Mexico on facilitating oil transfers to Cuba despite U.S. sanctions, and faced backlash following the admission.
Trump announced a three-day ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine running from May 9 to May 11, timed to coincide with Russia's Victory Day celebrations, along with a prisoner swap agreement.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio met with Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov and stated the U.S. is ready to help end the war in Ukraine, while cautioning that no quick deal is imminent and that progress depends on whether 'conditions and factors have changed.'

President Trump is scheduled to host Ukrainian President Zelensky at the White House on Tuesday, coinciding with Zelensky's attendance at memorial services for the late Sen. Lindsey Graham. Far-right influencer Laura Loomer met with Zelensky in Kyiv, reversing her longstanding public opposition to U.S. backing of Ukraine.
Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev, speaking alongside Russian President Vladimir Putin, called for a freeze of the war in Ukraine, according to Reuters.
The Kremlin stated it is too early to comment on reported U.S.-Ukraine negotiations regarding an air ceasefire, according to Reuters.
Ukrainian negotiator Sergiy Kyslytsya told NPR that Ukraine believes it has gained the leverage necessary to push Russia into serious negotiations, stating 'we have the upper hand.'

Zelenskyy met with President Trump at the White House and subsequently held meetings with U.S. senators on Capitol Hill. Trump is reported to have been impressed by Ukraine's military successes, contributing to an improved personal relationship between the two leaders, even as Ukraine continues to face sustained attacks.

Discussions at the White House meeting between Trump and Zelensky focused on licenses for Patriot interceptor missiles and diplomatic efforts related to the war, with both leaders describing the meeting positively.

Zelenskyy announced that Ukraine has submitted formal proposals to the United States aimed at ending the war with Russia, and warned that Russia may use its upcoming parliamentary elections as a pretext to declare a new mobilization.

French, German, and British diplomats are working to establish a format for future Russia-Ukraine peace negotiations, according to the NY Times, as European nations seek a defined role in eventual talks amid concerns about the Trump administration's approach.

Former Ukrainian defence chief Fedorov called for a wartime election, increasing political pressure on President Zelenskyy, though holding a vote remains a near-impossible logistical and security challenge amid ongoing Russian attacks, according to Al Jazeera.
A senior Russian diplomat stated that Russia is prepared to consider new peace proposals for Ukraine but indicated any plan would need to meet certain conditions, according to Reuters.
The leaders of France, Britain, and Germany are scheduled to co-chair a meeting on Ukraine on Monday, according to Reuters.
Tensions near the Strait of Hormuz have escalated, with one vessel seized near the UAE and taken toward Iran, and a second ship attacked and sunk off the coast of Oman.

Iran published a map asserting armed forces oversight over more than 22,000 square kilometers of the Strait of Hormuz. Despite regional tensions, OPEC+ leaders are expected to approve an increased oil output target for July, reflecting confidence in sustaining production increases.

Iran and Oman are in talks over a ship payment system related to the Strait of Hormuz, with the U.S. and Iran reported to remain far from a broader deal. Oil prices jumped as negotiations over reopening the strait reached an impasse, with disagreements persisting over Iran's uranium stockpile and proposed transit fees for the strait.

Iran and Oman have discussed establishing a toll system to charge vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz, a move that conflicts with Trump's stated opposition to transit fees on the strategic waterway. Iran's intensified closure of the strait has left sailors stranded, compounding hardships for those affected by the restrictions, according to Reuters.
Experts assess that full Iranian control over the Strait of Hormuz is unlikely, but Iran's attempts to charge vessels for passage have prompted concern within the international shipping industry.

U.S. Central Command announced it has redirected more than 100 commercial vessels as part of a naval blockade of Iranian ports in the Strait of Hormuz, describing the operation as involving more than 15,000 U.S. troops and launched in April at President Trump's direction.

Trump faces mounting pressure to reopen the Strait of Hormuz as Americans enter Memorial Day weekend with gas prices at their highest level in nearly four years, with Qatar and Pakistan acting as mediators applying pressure on Iran. British forces at Gibraltar are reported to be prepared to deploy autonomous mine-hunting equipment in the strait contingent on a peace agreement. BBC News recounted the story of Sunil Puniya, a crew member on his first sea job aboard the oil tanker Skylight, which was struck by a missile in the strait at the start of the Iran war, killing or leaving missing at least one crew member.

The U.S. and Iran reached a preliminary agreement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, but key issues including Iran's nuclear stockpile, uranium enrichment, and missile program were left unresolved and have not yet been formally discussed in negotiations, according to the NY Times. The timeline for resumption of normal shipping and oil price stabilization remains uncertain.

Despite a preliminary understanding between the U.S. and Iran on Strait of Hormuz reopening, the NY Times reported that no formal agreement on resuming normal shipping has been reached, leaving the timeline for restored traffic and oil price stabilization uncertain.

Maritime experts warned that even if a deal is reached to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, moving an estimated 1,500 backlogged ships stranded for nearly three months would be a complex and lengthy process.
A tanker reported an external explosion off the coast of Oman, according to the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO), which confirmed the crew is safe.
President Trump threatened serious repercussions if Iran and Oman proceeded with a deal to open the Strait of Hormuz, before adding 'They'll be fine,' according to the NY Times.

The U.S. Treasury Department sanctioned Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority (PGSA), a newly formed Iranian government agency, describing it as an IRGC attempt to control and monetize passage through the Strait of Hormuz.

Iran launched cruise missiles at two UAE tankers — the Mombasa and Al Bahiyah — in the Strait of Hormuz, killing one crew member, with the UAE Ministry of Defence confirming the attack. President Trump announced a 20% toll on all cargo transiting the Strait of Hormuz, a proposal the NY Times notes contradicts his administration's own position that such fees violate international law, while the New York Post reported the scheme could generate nearly $200 billion annually. Trump also demanded that wealthy Gulf oil-producing nations reimburse the U.S. for protecting ships in the strait. Oil prices surged to a one-month high, with Brent crude rising above $85 per barrel and WTI and Brent recording their largest two-day percentage gain in four months; Asian markets turned volatile in response to the proposed levy. A government report revealed the U.S. Strategic Petroleum Reserve is at precariously low stockpile levels and has suffered major equipment failures, leaks, and spills, raising energy security concerns.

Trump abandoned the proposed 20% Strait of Hormuz transit fee approximately 24 hours after announcing it on Tuesday, stating during a White House meeting with Iraq's prime minister that it would be replaced by investment deals with Gulf nations. The U.S. separately announced plans to reinstate a naval blockade over Iranian-controlled shipping in the strait. Iranian hardline lawmakers introduced a bill to formalize Iran's control over the Strait of Hormuz, aimed at undermining ongoing negotiations. Tensions in Yemen escalated following an Israeli strike on Sanaa Airport after an Iranian plane was diverted, prompting Houthi threats of retaliation and raising concerns that Houthi forces could attempt to block the Bab al-Mandeb strait. Iran also shifted focus to the Red Sea gateway as a new pressure point, according to Reuters. WTI crude rose to approximately $80 per barrel on Tuesday, its highest level in about a month.

Iran threatened to block all oil export routes in the region in response to the U.S. reimposition of a naval blockade on Iranian ports in the Strait of Hormuz, intensifying the standoff between the two countries.

President Trump suggested that pipelines in Texas and Alaska could serve as alternatives to the Strait of Hormuz, stating the strait is 'open if people want to go through it' despite Iranian officials continuing to impede maritime shipping through the waterway.

The U.S. military disabled the M/T Belma, a Curacao-flagged oil tanker, in the Arabian Sea on Wednesday after it attempted to sail to an Iranian port, marking the first vessel disabled since President Trump reimposed the naval blockade.

Iran has asked Yemen's Houthi movement to stand ready to close the Red Sea oil route if the United States strikes Iranian power infrastructure, according to Reuters, citing two senior Iranian sources and a regional source familiar with the matter. The request was discussed within Iranian leadership before being communicated to the Houthis. Pakistan separately expressed concern about being drawn into the U.S.-Iran conflict following Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia.

U.S. military forces boarded a sanctioned oil tanker in the Gulf of Oman. Chevron is set to sign oil deals with Iraq and back a pipeline project designed to bypass the Strait of Hormuz. IEA Executive Director Fatih Birol warned that a crisis in the strait threatens global energy security, calling on the world to be 'worried' if the situation does not improve.
Analysts warned that recognizing Iran's control over the Strait of Hormuz could set a dangerous precedent for other countries seeking to claim key global waterways.

The U.S. formally announced support for an Iraq-Syria pipeline rehabilitation agreement that would route crude exports from the Kirkuk oil fields to Syria's Baniyas port, with a U.S.-led international consortium to manage technical and financial aspects of the project. Chevron and ConocoPhillips were among U.S. firms signing oil-related agreements with Iraq at a U.S. Chamber of Commerce event, part of broader deal-making signaled by President Trump in the days prior.

Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz has effectively frozen following the seventh consecutive night of U.S. strikes on Iran, with an industry analyst telling CBS News that 'nobody is willing to move' through the waterway. The U.S. has reimposed a naval blockade on Iran's ports, with pressure expected to build on the Iranian public and global energy markets.

A London-based research group proposed forming a coalition of Gulf states to jointly share control of the Strait of Hormuz, using the now-defunct European Coal and Steel Community as a governance framework for the arrangement.
Al Jazeera reported on Iran attacking Kuwait infrastructure amid the ongoing conflict, raising concerns about broader Gulf security implications as regional tensions continue to escalate.
Iran's IRGC reported that two oil tankers exploded in the Strait of Hormuz after allegedly attempting to pass through what it described as an 'unsafe route,' according to state-run Fars News Agency.

Goldman Sachs analysts warned that oil prices could surpass $120 per barrel if disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz do not ease, projecting an average of $100 per barrel in the following year if traffic through the waterway remains affected. Yemen's Houthi rebels separately announced a naval blockade of the Bab Al-Mandeb Strait amid escalating U.S.-Iran tensions.

The Houthi movement warned shipping companies to avoid Saudi ports, prompting Saudi Arabia to condemn the blockade and warn of impacts on oil flows to importers worldwide. Two tankers carrying Saudi crude made U-turns in the Red Sea after receiving Houthi warnings. The Caspian Pipeline Consortium halted acceptance of Kazakh oil for export following tanker attacks.

Reuters reported that potential Houthi threats in the Red Sea would pose a significant challenge to an already stretched U.S. military. The Houthi declaration to block Red Sea oil routes threatens a key alternative shipping corridor Saudi Arabia has relied on heavily for exports since the Iran war began.

A Dubai-based logistics company announced a deal with the UAE on Wednesday to develop a new port system designed to bypass the Strait of Hormuz, according to the NY Times. Shipping tracking data showed an increasing number of vessels rerouting away from the Red Sea following Houthi threats, with multiple tankers making sharp U-turns; all had been traveling to or from Saudi ports before changing course. Approximately 6 million barrels of crude oil per day previously transiting the Bab al-Mandeb Strait to Asia are now at risk, raising questions about whether the Suez Canal can serve as an adequate alternative route for Asian oil consumers.

Yemen's Houthis claimed they carried out attacks on two Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea — the first strikes since the group announced its maritime embargo against Saudi Arabia. Oil prices climbed to a six-week high amid the escalating U.S.-Iran tensions.

Brent crude oil surpassed $100 per barrel following the confirmed strikes on two Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea, the first time the benchmark has crossed that threshold during the current crisis. Chinese refiners responded to mounting regional supply risks by securing increased volumes of Russian crude for September delivery and seeking additional Iranian oil supplies. Reuters sources reported that Iran flew IRGC commanders and missile equipment to Houthi forces in Yemen, representing a significant transfer of military personnel and materiel to the group responsible for the tanker attacks.

Houthi forces formally imposed a blockade on the Bab al-Mandeb strait, and UN Yemen envoy Hans Grundberg expressed alarm, warning further confrontation risks deepening Yemeni suffering and calling for de-escalation talks. Tankers rerouting to avoid both the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandeb now face approximately one additional month of transit time and costs of around $2.5 million per voyage. Oil prices were on track for a weekly gain driven by the Red Sea shipping disruptions and output cuts in Kazakhstan, with Brent above $100 per barrel triggering a sell-off in U.S. markets and subsequent declines in Asian stocks amid concerns over rising borrowing costs.
A tanker switched its Asia voyage to route via the Suez Canal amid continued Houthi militant warnings, according to the vessel's owner, underscoring the ongoing disruption to Red Sea shipping routes.

The U.S. military reported disabling a tanker attempting to evade the American blockade on Iranian ports. A Greek-operated air defense system shot down missiles over Saudi Arabia, according to Reuters. The U.S. and UK are reportedly planning a summit focused on shipping security in the Strait of Hormuz, according to Newsmax. Dozens of ships continued to traverse the Red Sea despite the Houthi blockade, though scattered disruptions and uncertainty about safe passage persisted, according to the New York Times.

Scientists warned that ships stalled near the Strait of Hormuz due to conflict-related traffic blockages could trigger an invasive species ecological catastrophe. Houthi military spokesperson Brig. Gen. Yahya Saree announced the group had fired missiles and drones at Saudi Arabia, claiming the strikes were retaliation for Saudi airstrikes on Hodeida.

Houthi forces claimed to have targeted Saudi Aramco oil facilities along the Red Sea, with Saudi Arabia and Houthi rebels exchanging fire in what NBC News describes as a new warfront in the Middle East.
Talks between Oman and Iran on reopening the Strait of Hormuz and their respective territorial waterways have made progress, according to two sources cited by CBS News.
Iran-backed Houthi forces exploited a period of Saudi reluctance toward military engagement to pressure Riyadh for political concessions in Yemen, according to the NY Times.

Iran claimed Monday that it controls the Strait of Hormuz and forced back six ships attempting to transit without clearance, according to Iranian state media citing an unidentified source. Ship traffic through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait dropped to just 11 cargo vessels — the lowest in months — following Houthi attacks on Saudi oil depots along the Red Sea, according to analytics platform Kpler. Saudi Arabia announced it destroyed drones launched by Iran-backed groups in Iraq, and separately blamed Iran-backed militias based in Iraq for additional drone attacks, drawing the kingdom deeper into the wider regional conflict as it faces simultaneous pressure from both Iraq and Yemen.
Iran's Foreign Minister held discussions with his Saudi Arabian and Omani counterparts regarding security in the Strait of Hormuz, according to Reuters.

Iran and Oman exchanged formal proposals on managing the Strait of Hormuz, with the Omani proposal modeled on the Strait of Malacca system under which transiting ships would pay voluntary fees; Iran subsequently rejected the proposal. The Houthi group claimed responsibility for a missile strike on a Saudi oil tanker in the Red Sea, escalating their declared naval blockade of Saudi shipping, as fighting between Saudi Arabia and Houthi forces intensified in a new wave of attacks.

Yemen's Houthi group is reportedly considering imposing fees on commercial ships sailing through the southern Red Sea, according to sources cited by the New York Post, coming one week after the group declared a naval blockade on Saudi Arabia. The NY Times reported that attacks on ships in both the Strait of Hormuz and the Bab al-Mandab Strait are spreading shipping risks across multiple critical Middle East oil routes.

Two tankers, including a U.S. gas storage tanker, were struck in an apparent drone attack at a port on Egypt's Mediterranean coast, causing fires aboard both vessels. Saudi Arabia is seeking to build an international coalition to safeguard Red Sea shipping as Houthi strikes on energy tankers expand. Asian nations including Japan are turning to Canadian crude via the Trans Mountain Expansion pipeline amid Strait of Hormuz supply uncertainty, while QatarEnergy purchased 33 U.S. LNG cargoes to offset potential Hormuz disruption.

An attack struck an Egyptian port near the Suez Canal, according to the NY Times, compounding concerns about the vulnerability of the critical waterway through which a significant share of global shipping passes.

Iran claimed it targeted U.S. facilities in Kuwait and struck two tankers in the Strait of Hormuz that were operating under U.S. aerial escort, according to CBS News. ExxonMobil and Chevron reported combined Q2 profits of approximately $26.5 billion — a more than 300% increase from the previous quarter — as rising energy prices driven by the ongoing conflict boosted earnings.

Yemen's Houthi movement denied reports that it plans to charge fees for ships transiting the Red Sea, stating the route remains free. The UKMTO reported two separate tanker incidents off the coast of Oman.

A Qatari-flagged LNG tanker, the Gaslog Shanghai, was struck by a missile while transiting the Strait of Hormuz, sustaining damage to its engine room and becoming inoperable off the Omani coast. Iran issued warnings of wider disruption to shipping in the waterway. U.S. embassies in the region simultaneously began urging Americans to leave the Middle East.

Satellite images revealed the sanctioned vessel Caroline Bezengi, reportedly carrying over 800,000 barrels of Russian crude, is leaking oil into a marine reserve off the Omani coast home to endangered wildlife. Iranian negotiators reportedly signaled to the U.S. that they would reopen the Strait of Hormuz before Trump called off planned strikes, though Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps denied any such deal and dismissed Trump's pullback announcement as 'psychological operations.' Experts warned that Secretary of State Rubio's plan to bypass the Strait faces significant obstacles, including pipeline capacity limitations and ongoing Red Sea security threats. An Italian-led EU naval force boarded a sanctioned Russian shadow fleet tanker in the Mediterranean Sea.

Analysts warn that threats to oil tankers in the Middle East have reached their worst level since the start of the Iran war, with fresh attacks on alternative shipping routes leaving tankers navigating an increasingly complex threat environment, according to BBC News.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations Center reported a vessel was struck by an 'unknown projectile' in the Strait of Hormuz, causing oil prices to rise. Thousands of civilian sailors remain stranded on ships in the strait amid risk of Iranian attack, with crew members on at least one vessel having been held by the Iranian navy for more than three months, according to the NY Times.

Iran and Oman are reportedly close to an agreement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, with both countries expected to collect a service fee covering environmental and security costs, according to the New York Post. U.S. Secretary of State Rubio and Treasury Secretary Bessent announced that talks had progressed toward reopening the waterway, causing oil prices to fall.

Iran reported that talks with Oman over the Strait of Hormuz are proceeding 'positively,' while US officials indicated a deal could be possible soon. A ship was also reported struck in the Red Sea amid the ongoing regional tensions.

Iran announced it is nearing a final agreement with Oman on an acceptable route for ships through the Strait of Hormuz, a deal that would effectively ratify Tehran's control over the waterway, according to the NY Times. Trump stated 'a lot of progress has been made' on reopening the strait and suggested a deal could be announced as early as Wednesday.

Iran and Oman reached a formal agreement on shipping routes through the Strait of Hormuz, according to Al Jazeera. Eight major shipping organisations signed a joint letter opposing proposed tolls on the strait, warning that such fees would harm livelihoods worldwide. Gulf shipping traffic declined after Houthi forces claimed to have attacked a Saudi tanker, per Reuters. Oil prices fell following the Iran-Oman talks amid hopes for a broader US-Iran peace deal.

The shipping industry has deemed a proposed deal for passage through the Strait of Hormuz not feasible, according to Reuters sources. Trump denied that U.S. munitions stockpiles are running low, described them as 'massive,' and characterized those who leaked information about stockpile levels to news outlets as 'treasonous,' vowing to pursue them.

Oman and Iran confirmed agreement on specific geographic coordinates for a maritime route through the Strait of Hormuz, though broader negotiations extended past the Thursday deadline expected by President Trump. Oil prices rose amid ongoing concerns over plans to reopen the strait, according to Reuters.

The US expressed expectation of an imminent Strait of Hormuz deal, while Sunni powers announced a united defense pact, according to Reuters. Negotiations between Iran and Oman are continuing with no formal agreement yet announced, according to CBS News.

Iran's Supreme National Security Council head announced the Strait of Hormuz will remain closed until the United States meets specific conditions, with Iran issuing a formal list of demands that dampened hopes for an imminent reopening. The UAE separately reported a ship was targeted in the region. Iran-backed Houthi rebels also launched drone and missile attacks on Saudi military targets in Marib, Yemen, killing two people and wounding more than a dozen others.

Vice President JD Vance stated that 'some progress over the last few days' has been made in Iran-Oman negotiations over the strait. Iran's IRGC set conditions for reopening the waterway, demanding an end to the US blockade, while the US sought commitments from Tehran to cease attacks on ships. Tanker industry representatives described ships in the region as remaining in limbo, with transit still dangerous and a formal agreement described as far away.

Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi stated Sunday that there are no ongoing negotiations between Tehran and Washington, even as Iran claimed a Hormuz deal is in its 'final stages' but conditioned on US action. According to the NY Times, Iran is leveraging control of the strait to press Washington into releasing frozen assets, lifting sanctions, and ending its naval blockade, pushing for a return to a June memorandum of understanding.

Oil prices rose amid continued uncertainty over a Strait of Hormuz reopening, according to Reuters. CBS News reported that U.S. gas prices have risen more than $1 since the conflict with Iran began, compounding financial pressure on American consumers alongside increased Pentagon spending. Iran's Revolutionary Guard confirmed the strait will remain closed until the U.S. meets demands that include payment for war damages.

An Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman stated that Oman-mediated talks on shipping routes are 'separate' from negotiations to fully reopen the Strait of Hormuz, signaling Iran intends to keep the waterway closed until the Trump administration meets its broader demands.

Gulf shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz fell to just six vessels, according to Reuters, indicating a significant reduction in maritime activity. A deal between Iran and Oman to reopen the strait remains at risk, as Iran reiterated the waterway will only reopen once the United States meets Tehran's broader demands.

Oil prices rose to $90 a barrel as the Hormuz stalemate deepened and commercial shipping traffic in the strait dwindled further, according to the NY Times. Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi reiterated Tuesday that Iran will not reopen the strait until the U.S. meets its conditions, as Trump separately demanded compensation from Iran for 'all of the people that they have killed.' A U.S. military helicopter fired on a merchant vessel's rudder to disable it after the crew ignored multiple warnings while attempting to cross the U.S. blockade, according to a U.S. official cited by the Wall Street Journal.

A Houthi strike on the Egyptian-owned cargo vessel Tihamah in the Bab al-Mandeb strait killed six people and wounded 10, marking the first lethal Houthi attack on shipping since the outbreak of the US-Iran conflict, according to Yemen's government and the Washington Examiner. The vessel was set ablaze, with footage circulating showing the ship in flames. The IEA cut its 2026 oil supply forecast as the Strait of Hormuz reopening remains elusive, according to Reuters. Iran's top security official again declared the strait will not reopen unless the U.S. meets Tehran's conditions, as Pakistan's Naqvi visited Tehran.

Gulf oil exporters are investing billions of dollars in infrastructure to create alternative export routes bypassing the Strait of Hormuz, reflecting growing concerns about the waterway's strategic vulnerability, according to the NY Times. Analysts told Fox News that Houthi attacks on Red Sea shipping may prompt the US to forge closer ties with Somaliland amid concerns over Djibouti's reliability and China's expanding presence in the region.

Tehran asserted the Strait of Hormuz is under Iranian control, while Trump countered by claiming the U.S. has 'total control' over the waterway, marking a direct exchange of opposing claims over the strait's sovereignty. Oil prices fell as lower demand forecasts weighed on markets, even as U.S.-Iran nuclear talks remained deadlocked.
Iran-backed Houthi rebels clashed with Yemeni government forces, according to AP News, amid the broader regional conflict.

Iran attacked two ADNOC vessels in the Strait of Hormuz with no injuries reported. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth declared the U.S. can sustain its naval blockade against Iran indefinitely, and oil prices steadied following the announcement. The USS Abraham Lincoln is departing the Middle East amid reports of poor living conditions for sailors and marines aboard, while the USS George Washington has departed Vietnam and is heading to the region as a carrier rotation. Vice President JD Vance stated that keeping gas prices low is 'goal number one' in the Iran war, and the White House addressed competing U.S.-Iran claims over control of the Strait of Hormuz.
The US warned Iran it would increase economic pressure after two more ships were attacked in the Strait of Hormuz, according to Reuters.
UAE authorities formally attributed Thursday's drone strikes on the two ADNOC-managed tankers to Iran, confirming the attack was carried out by Iranian drones.

Trump stated on Friday he would declare the Strait of Hormuz U.S. territory and posted at least one AI-generated image of himself seizing an Iranian oil tanker. Iran rejected the assertion, with Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi posting a statement on X calling the comments 'fanciful delusions.' Separately, the UAE accused Iran of attacking a third ADNOC vessel in the Strait of Hormuz within a week, with the latest strike occurring Friday as the ship transited the strait. Yemen's Mocha port halted operations after Houthi attacks, according to the port director, marking a significant disruption to the Red Sea coastal facility.

Iran struck a fourth ship in the Strait of Hormuz, according to CBS News, following three earlier drone strikes on ADNOC-managed vessels within the same week. Lebanese health authorities reported Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon killed at least 11 people, including children.

Iran-backed Houthis are reportedly exploiting Yemen's fractured state to threaten the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, raising concerns the waterway could become a second critical maritime chokepoint alongside the Strait of Hormuz.

Oil prices held steady and shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz slowed following the recent wave of tanker attacks, according to Reuters data tracking vessel movements. Diego Garcia has been described by a U.S. official as 'integral' to supporting carrier strike groups and regional supply chains after Iran's earlier strike on Bahrain forced the Pentagon to shift its logistics hub there, according to Fox News.

Houthi forces claimed responsibility for attacking Saudi vessels off the coast of Mocha, Yemen, and for a missile strike on a Saudi vessel in the Red Sea, according to Reuters. Houthi and Yemeni government forces also exchanged drone attacks, marking a tactical shift as both sides demonstrated growing aerial drone capabilities, according to Al Jazeera. Iran threatened to go on the offensive in the Strait of Hormuz if diplomacy with the United States fails.

A vessel was struck by an unknown projectile in the Strait of Hormuz, resulting in one casualty and damage to the ship's engine room, according to UKMTO. Trump threatened to bomb Oman if it interferes in potential negotiations over Hormuz control. Oil markets have begun pricing in a prolonged crisis in the strait, signaling trader expectations of an extended disruption to the critical shipping route.

Trump posted a map on Truth Social labeling the Strait of Hormuz as 'new US territory' and separately stated no talks or conversations with Iran are ongoing or scheduled, while claiming the strait is 'open and operating.' A second vessel was struck by an unknown projectile exiting the strait on Tuesday, again affecting the ship's engine room, according to UKMTO. The NY Times reported that at least 17 commercial sailors have been killed in and around Iranian and Omani waters since March, six months into the conflict. Saudi Arabia and the UAE are pushing to expand oil stockpiles in Japan and South Korea as the conflict threatens regional supply routes.

The U.S. Navy has been conducting covert operations to escort oil tankers through the Strait of Hormuz, according to the NY Times, as Iranian threats have rendered the waterway increasingly dangerous for energy exports.

Yemen's Houthi forces claimed responsibility for attacks on Najran airport and Saudi Aramco facilities in Saudi Arabia, according to Reuters. Romania destroyed a marine drone discovered near the Neptun Deep gas project in the Black Sea, according to the country's minister.

A spike in 'dark' oil tankers navigating the Strait of Hormuz with their location devices switched off has been reported, as vessels attempt to evade Iranian attacks; the NY Times noted the trend raises the risk of collisions and catastrophic oil spills.
NATO member states are holding discussions on options regarding the Strait of Hormuz, according to Reuters, with talks occurring outside formal NATO alliance structures.
Iran granted permission for a number of Iraqi oil tankers to pass through the Strait of Hormuz, according to Reuters.

Iran published a vessel blacklist for the Strait of Hormuz, warning that ships on the list are subject to seizure, in what Newsweek described as an escalation of Tehran's efforts to control the waterway. Iran's parliament also advanced a draft law that would require ships from permitted countries transiting the strait to pay service fees to Iran.

An oil tanker was struck near the Strait of Hormuz overnight following Iran's vow to retaliate against the US over recently imposed sanctions. Reports of Iran-Oman talks on a possible temporary deal for the strait drove US oil prices lower, with West Texas Intermediate and Brent crude's October contracts declining by nearly 7% and 9% respectively over five days. The US threatened sanctions against any country or entity engaging with Iran's gold, digital assets, aviation, shipping, and technology industries. Saudi Arabia rerouted its oil exports away from both the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea, redirecting shipments through the Suez Canal.

Iran and Oman reached a formal agreement establishing a temporary corridor in the Strait of Hormuz, including a revenue-sharing arrangement, with Iran's Revolutionary Guards announcing the deal. Oil prices fell for a third consecutive day as the agreement sparked renewed optimism in global energy markets.
Oil prices extended their losses as expectations grew that diplomatic talks could further ease supply disruptions stemming from Middle East tensions, according to Reuters.
Iran has conditioned implementation of the temporary Strait of Hormuz shipping corridor on the United States meeting a series of unspecified demands, according to the Washington Examiner.

U.S. CENTCOM Admiral Brad Cooper disclosed a classified mission in which Navy divers, SEALs, and air power were used to clear Iranian sea mines from shipping lanes in the Strait of Hormuz, according to Fox News.

Analysts assessed as implausible U.S. claims that Iran could use rockets to mine the Strait of Hormuz, though experts noted Iran has a history of adapting conventional weapons for unconventional purposes, according to Al Jazeera.

Two tankers were struck in the Strait of Hormuz, pushing global oil prices above $90 per barrel, with WTI and Brent crude contracts reaching their highest levels in nearly two weeks. Shipping data showed commodity vessel transits through the strait remaining in single digits.
